posts.title: Gross-up NI and Tax functionality
posts.details:
For example a customer might want to add a cash payment that was given to an employee for £500 so they will add £500 on a net to gross payment type and the system will add the £500 plus a gross top-up for tax and NI based on that individual?

posts.title: Manager approval for cancelling holiday requests on ESS
posts.details:
Hi there, we recently turned on holiday booking on ESS. Teams like it, but it is causing a few operational difficulties that employees can cancel holidays on the app without a manager's approval.  Sometimes at key holiday times, there is a bit of negotiation within a team to spread out holidays so that you are not, for example, left without chefs. Then, if one of those chefs cancels a negotiated holiday, this causes knock on effects on the rest of the team, and holiday days for the chef build up and have to be taken later.

We would like to see manager approval for cancellations the same way as for bookings, so that the manager can have a conversation with their team.

posts.title: Holiday Requests: A New Calendar Format with Ability to Approve/Decline Holidays
posts.details:
Hi Team at Fourth,

We would like to see the holiday requests on the calendar as per image attached.

This 'Calendar Format' would allow us to view the holiday accrued to date, as well as the holiday days paid already taken. We would not want to run the risk of authorizing holiday days to an employee who has already overtaken a considerable amount of holidays.

In this format, we would also be able to see the 'Holiday Days Paid' or 'Half Holiday Days Paid' already approved appearing in blue(e.g. Michael Jackson; e.g. Roger Federer)
The Holiday Days or Half Holiday Days not yet addressed by a Manager, would appear in yellow (e.g. Helen Mirren, e.g. Whitney Houston) .
In this format, we would also be able to see which holiday days have been requested as 'paid' and which ones as 'unpaid' (currently this difference does not appear on the calendar)

What we would also like to be able to do is hovering over the holiday day requested on the calendar and being able to see on which date the employee had requested this holiday (as you know, especially in certain period of the year, e.g. Christmas, we can receive several holiday days requests by multiple employees for the same period. We would normally approve the holidays based on a first-come, first-served basis)

Ultimately, we would like to have the ability of clicking on the day in the calendar and being given automatically the option of 'authorizing' or 'declining' the request, & clicking 'Save'.

This method would allow us to have better control of the multiple holiday requests in a same period, their approval/decline as well as the current status of holiday allowance.

Could this be an option?

posts.title: Include Paid Holidays in Flexible Holiday Rota Details Screen
posts.details:
When selecting the 'i' icon next to Avg Hours/Week in the Holiday screen, the Days and Hours only include those where the employee has worked a shift.
Since paid holidays are included in the calculation of Avg Days/Week (and therefore Days Allowed), this can lead to confusion when only viewing the Flexible Holiday Rota Details screen. If you wanted to manually calculate you would need to go through the employees' holidays which can be time-consuming and can lead to user errors.
It would be beneficial if the days could include paid holidays or even better if there was a separate column for paid holidays on this screen.

posts.title: Hard Restrictions surrounding rest periods  - working time directive
posts.details:
We would like you to implement a hard restriction to ensure UK customers can comply with working time directive for young workers. 

The below rest periods are currently covered under the option of a soft warning but we would like these as hard restrictions

  • 12 hours' rest in any 24-hour period in which they work (for example, between one working day and the next)
  • 48 hours' (2 days) rest taken together, each week or – if there is a good business reason why this is not possible – at least 36 hours' rest, with the remaining 12 hours taken as soon as possible afterwards

Thanks

Leanne

posts.title: T&A Breaks Data
posts.details:
Hello

Would be great if we could get additional column on the Analytics page of T&A to show the total amount of time taken in breaks. This would be the missing link of data. It would also highlight if the differences between forecast and actuals is due to increased hours or due to breaks.

For example (break taken)

  • Total T&A Hours for a 12-6 shift = 6 hours
  • T&A Break 30 mins or 0.5 hours
  • total Actual hours = 5.5 hours

Example (no break taken)

  • Total T&A Hours for a 12-6 shift = 6 hours
  • T&A Break = 0
  • total Actual hours = 6 hours

This would allow us to identify where breaks are being taken and are not. This helps ensure that team are rested or where team are potentially taking breaks but no logging them meaning we are potentially over paying for hours that have not been worked.

Being able to review this at an organisational level would also be required to spot themes/trends and compliance

Example

  • 2000 hours worked in a week
  • 10 hours of breaks
  • Would identify that breaks are either not being taken or are not be recorded on T&A

Thanks

Graeme

PizzaExpress

posts.title: Ability to bulk publish recipes from RME to Inventory
posts.details:
Currently there is no functionality to bulk publish standard recipes from RME to Inventory and this would be hugely beneficial if this could be developed.

When we open a new location we have in the region of 1000 unique standard recipes that currently have to manually published one by one, which can take many days.

comments.author: Michael Hordern
comments.body:
Hi Adam, Thanks for sharing this. 

The good news is that this is something that we have already been thinking about.

Part of the appeal of a mobile solution for me, beyond just freeing users from their desktops and offices, was about using the built-in features of these devices - like GPS, push notifications and of course the camera - to do clever stuff!

The addition last year of barcode scanning to the Counting app (for hotel & leisure customers using Adaco) was exactly the sort of thing we wanted to be able to do, and extending it to Ordering and Receiving feels like a great idea.

But you tell me...?! 

If other Adaco customers in hotel & leisure think adding barcode scanning to Ordering and Receiving has value then please up-vote Adam's idea. And it would be great if you could also share a comment as to why. 

And if customers in other sectors like restaurants and catering would also like to see barcode scanning capabilities in their Fourth Inventory mobile apps then please let us know in the comments.

comments.author: Michael Hordern
comments.body:
Scanning Prototypes

Further to my comment last week, I'm pleased to announce that our UX (User eXperience) team have created two online prototypes for what barcode scanning in Ordering and Receiving could look like.

More than that they've also shared the prototypes in the SelfTest tool (from Lookback) so that you can not only see, but also interact with, what they've been working on.  The app allows you to share your experiences and thoughts with the team and genuinely participate in the refinement of the final product.

We hope you'll find it an interesting experience, please give it a try (and vote for this idea).

User Testing of the Barcode functionality

You can find links to the tests below and can participate yourself or send them to a colleague. You'll find simple instructions to setup, record and upload your experiences. There is also a survey at the end of the test for your feedback. The testing can be done at any time that's convenient to you.

  • Ordering - https://participate.lookback.io/HKXcuY   
  • Receiving - https://participate.lookback.io/DqdMa5   

Note: If you try to open these links from your PC it won't work as the tests can only be done on mobile.

If you've got any questions or want to know more then please reply here or contact your account manager.

posts.title: Ordering App - Identify Preferred Supply Option, or ONLY show Preferred Supply Option
posts.details:
This idea is to have two new organsation configuration options in Inventory that dictate behaviour in the Ordering App:

1. Identify preferred product OR

2. Show preferred product only

This is due to ongoing supply chain issues, leading to multiple product options being listed for each site (see image example).

 

Preferred is already defined in two ways:

1. Non site recipe recost organisations: Highest ranked product

2. Site recipe recost organisations: Highest ranked available supplier/product combination by site

 

Requested behaviour in Ordering App:

1. Identify preferred product:

Where multiple options are available for the same product (alternates), some kind of badge/icon that clearly identifies which option is the preferred option.

Where there are not multiple options, there is no need to display the preferred badge/icon.

2. Show preferred product only:

Where multiple options are available for the same product (alternates), only display the preferred product option, hiding all others from view/search.

 

This will enable customers to be able to switch between different supply options on a daily/weekly basis as thye manage ongoing supply issues and availability.

 

Obviosuly, customers would need to ensure they are accurately managing their alternate rankings where either of these options are in use.

Thanks

comments.author: Andrew Barber
comments.body:
Hi 397187087332,

The rank is taken into consideration when applying the cost model. The ranking set in RME should be the order in which preferance of purchase should be applied. In the case of the preferred supplier cost model, if the top ranked supplier is not available to site then the alternate from the highest rank from an available supplier is used in determining theoretical cost.

One reason for not basing on the item purchases is that it may not be reflective of the optimal way in which the item should be used, i.e. preffered supplier, for example if consistently purchasing from a supplier or configuration that does not represent best value or alignment with organisation preference.

You're suggesting another type of cost model, i.e. to base on last cost price paid, however this could have it's own challenges, e.g. where an item is purchased at a significantly higher or lower price relative to other purchases in the period based on alternates available and therefore could result in similar variances. Perhaps setting a site level preference on rank could be another approach here?

We'll leave this idea open pending input and voting from other customers!

 

Thanks,

Andrew Barber - Product Manager: Restaurant Inventory

comments.author: Emily Scott
comments.body:
Hello,

is there any update on what is happening with the continuous service date field? It's causing us major issue with the integrity of our data and I previously raised it and was told the idea was already raised via here hence why I am commenting on this. 

Here's a breakdown: 

The continuous service date is a read only field - it needs to be more than this and used to calculate statutory payments (SMP, SPP etc) and holiday entitlement, CSP entitlement etc instead of the Payroll Start Date. The Payroll Start Date should be the start date of the payroll for that particular entity. 

We have multiple entities where we may find employees moving from one entity to another. The issue we face is because currently the payroll start date stipulates all of the above, we have to change the payroll start date to the continuous service date to ensure all length of service entitlement calculations are correct. I.E if someone started on 7th May 2023, and moved to a new entity on 7th May 2024, we have to make the Payroll Start date 7th May 2023 (even though that isn't the payroll start date for the new location) because the continuous service date doesn't feed into the relevant payroll and entitlements calculations. 

This causes us issues with our data, the reporting is completely incorrect as it will look at an employee starting at a location from the payroll start date when they didn't. Currently I'm trying to work out labour turnover for the last 5 years and it is so painful because of the workaround we've had to make because Fourth won't offer a solution for us.

It causes issues with the integration of Flow as it duplicates records, having two records, one with a termination date causing the record on flow to be deactivated. We currently have a work around to put an X at the front - but yet again another workaround because Fourth won't address the issue (which I have raised continuously). 

It's great to see the things Fourth are advertising via their roadmap new and exciting initiatives - but this is a fairly easy fix for a fairly significant problem and it's concerning that an idea was raised 3 years ago and hasn't been addressed. It's a real basic need so I struggle to understand why it can't be addressed fairly quickly. 

It needs fixed - make the continuous service date actually be the continuous service date and not a pointless field! 

391566916951 - fyi, this really needs fixed. It's really causing a lot more work internally than we would anticipate given Fourth should be sophisticated enough to handle this.

comments.author: Fourth Customer Success Portal
comments.body:
Hi 16887120049549,

Thanks for your detailed post/description here. Sorry to hear it's causing so much inconvenience for you. Our product team have been in contact with Flow, and we are expecting them to change their integration to use the UK Employee API (which has the correct fields). This would then address these matters. We will let you know as soon as we can what the status of this is.

Fourth Communities Team

comments.author: Michael Hordern
comments.body:
Hi Paul,

We've been discussing this question.  We think it is a useful change that would help more than one customer and would like to try and schedule it next year (subject to size and capacity).

However, there is some complexity in how we might deliver this enhancement and it would be useful to get some customer views on the options we are considering.

A market list can either be private or shared.  A private list is only visible to its “owner” and can only be modified or deleted by that person.  Currently, shared lists are visible to all users at that location but only the “owner” of the market list is allowed to modify or delete a shared list.  In most cases the owner of the list is the person that created it.

The request is to allow “Shared Ownership” of market lists, which we interpret as allowing some or all other users at a location to modify (and delete) shared lists.  This may be because the original owner has left or because creating lists is seen as a collaborative activity.

Option 1 for this enhancement is to simply remove the owner-checking completely for all customers and allow any users at that location to modify or delete any shared list. 

  • This is the most straightforward approach and requires no additional admin of user roles or permissions. 
  • It does however mean that product lines and even whole lists might be removed in error by anyone with access to the app. 
  • This option would immediately change the experience for all customers; in which case it might be considered too straightforward by some of you...

Option 2 is to add specific user-level access rights for “modify…” and “delete shared market lists”

  • These would be configured on/off by profile in Inventory, Adaco or Trade Simple and applied to each user automatically. 
  • The default would be “off” for both settings and the system would continue to behave as now for all customers, until the new configuration was applied to their users. 
  • For example: the “GM” and “AGM” roles might be given permission to delete and modify shared lists, “Chef” and “Bar Manager” roles might be given permission to only modify shared lists, but everyone else (at this customer) cannot. 
  • Lists and products might still be removed in error but by fewer users. 
  • This is the most complicated option from a development and management/admin POV.

Other potential options might include combinations of customer-level settings and user-level access rights for “modify…” and “delete” or new market lists types/statuses.  However, these would require at least equivalent development effort to Option 2 and would increase the management/admin complexity, but probably wouldn’t add much value in my view.

Private lists would remain as now.

What do other customers using market lists in the ordering app think?

comments.author: Rebecca Mecomber
comments.body: This has been a continuing ask by our operators.  When team members leave us their lists are still shared and we have no way to delete them.  This causes a lot of confusion within the management teams as to which lists to use.  Having one shared list is easier for the sites to manage; as they only have one set of lists to go in and update when products change, new items are added, or we have an upcoming LTO that require it's own products.  While I completely understand where this could cause issues with some other customers, if we made it user/permissions based then you would eliminate a lot of those concerns.  The role/permissions could be given to the administers or Super Users at the very least.  Thanks!

posts.title: Ordering - access baskets created by other users at the same location
posts.details: If I create an order on the app I want my colleagues to be able to access that order, so that they can add products and send it when required.  This is possible to do on the core system but we want to be able to do it on the app too.  The ability to make the order available to others would ideally be an option selected per order, rather than as default for all orders in a basket.
posts.author: Simeon Maas

comments.author: Michael Hordern
comments.body:
Hi Simeon,

This "shared basket" idea has been suggested to us in the past (before we had this Ideas portal) and while we can see the possible benefit of multiple people working on an order before it is sent - adding what they need before someone finally sends the whole thing off - in theory, I'm concerned that it might make things too complicated in practice:

  • What's to stop a given user just deciding to send it, before everyone else is ready?  
  • What's to stop one user deleting or reducing another user's part of the order?
  • What if everyone assumes someone else is responsible for sending the final order and it doesn't get sent before the cut off time?
  • etc.

If the answer to these questions is "just ask them", couldn't they also just ask "anything you need from this supplier today?" ;)

Of course we could build new rules and functionality into the basket to stop these problems but someone would have to maintain these and deal with the cases where something needed overriding or changing.  It feels like too much IMHO!

It starts to feel a bit like the "requisition and purchase order" functionality that our Adaco product has for use in hotels - lots of people want to contribute their needs to a final order - they raise requisitions - and one person has the job of collating and sending these off to the supplier as a PO.  Adaco has routing and approval functionality to support that flow (and it doesn't allow shared shopping baskets).

However, my feeling is that restaurants are - in general - a bit less complex than hotels.  I guess the number of people contributing to a single order is significantly lower and that most orders (as you suggest) probably don't need this at all - just sometimes.

But it would be great to hear from others: Do you need this "shared basket" functionality from our ordering app?  Under what circumstances would you use it? 

Get voting (up or down)!

posts.title: SSO- Allow extra layer of security e.g. PIN to access HR/Payroll apps when users also have Inventory
posts.details:
Many customers will have users logging into both HR and Payroll as well as Inventory via SSO. This works well if users have and use their own devices as the risk of users forgetting to logout and someone having access to view their HR details is minimised. 

For many customers, they require their teams to use shared devices when carrying out tasks relating to their jobs e.g.  using the stock counting apps. Using shared devices, which is business policy, with one login significantly increases the risk of a user seeing another users personal details which will breach GDPR and causes all sorts practical issues at site and for head office. In these times of resourcing difficulty , the customer cannot afford such incidents. 

SSO is the right way to do things, it ensures users, once terminated, no longer have access to data they shouldn't see. So, to ensure this can always be the way users are set up, would it be possible for Fourth to devise a means to add the option of another security layer on the HR and Payroll apps e.g. a pin?

Adding a secondary security measure for users of both HR and P2P to the engage app I feel removes the risk of users seeing one anothers sensitive data. Once a user adopts inventory or HR, they can add another password/pin/passcode to HR and Payroll apps should a user pick up a device with their personal session open. 

This would avoid users having two instances of engage and two usernames and passwords as is currently the issue for wagamama which also adds the overhead of having to manually deactivate a user in Inventory when they leave the business. 

Thanks,

Carol

posts.title: My Schedules Functionality
posts.details:
Hi

Currently when an unavailability request is approved or rejected by a manager in My Schedules no record of the actioned request is kept in the "Resolved" section of the Team Requests on the app. If a request was approved in error there is no way to correct this by the manager - for example a recurring Saturday off request is approved but the manager only intended to approve one of the days. The team member now has unavailability approved for every Saturday and the manager is unable to correct it via the app.

Also additional reporting on My Schedules requests would be useful so that senior management can track who is sending in requests, the status of the requests and who approved the requests and when. Currently anyone with access to the location/division can approve an employee request with no audit as to who approved.

Thanks

Rebecca

Are you able to provide more detail on the business need that the calculation of recipe 'High Fat, Salt and Sugar' (HFSS) scores would be meeting for your restaurants? 

Having reviewed the regulation guidance, it seems that restaurants are not in scope for the related legislation about 'promotions restrictions' apart from free refill restrictions on prepared soft drinks containing added sugar ingredients.

posts.title: Approval Workflow Considerations
posts.details:
We would like to submit the following for consideration with respect to approval workflows:

1) Activate all steps in an approval route when the document is first submitted - this will allow all approvers access to the document and assist with pushing documents through for those who may not view their approval queue as often.

2) Allow a document to progress through final approval without the review step being completed.  We do not find a difference currently between reviewing and approving as neither allow the document to progress through the workflow until review is complete.

3) when setting up an approval route, alert the person entering if a reviewer/approver does not have access to the department they are requesting approval.  In our case, the document sat in queue for some time because the reviewer couldn't see it (did not have access to the department) and it was not active for anyone else in the route.

4) regardless of notification settings per user, a global feature which would send an email every day to a user who has a document outstanding in an approval route.  It simply falls out of mind for many users if they don't immediately act on an app or other communication.

5) allow approvals to be setup by account number and/or department.  Allowing this with and/or logic would eliminate many of the challenges we are having with approvals currently.

posts.title: T&A Scheduling report
posts.details:
Hello,

An idea to have an additional column on the T&A Report regarding breaks

Schedules > Reporting > T&A report

At present the T&A breaks are bundled together behind the time of the break which makes it hard to extract the data from

Ideally there would be an additional column similar to Total Forecast Hours, Total T&A Hours and Total Actual Hours

For example (break taken)

  • Total T&A Hours for a 12-6 shift = 6 hours
  • T&A Break 30 mins or 0.5 hours
  • total Actual hours = 5.5 hours

Example (no break taken)

  • Total T&A Hours for a 12-6 shift = 6 hours
  • T&A Break = 0
  • total Actual hours = 6 hours

This would allow us to identify where breaks are being taken and are not. This helps ensure that team are rested or where team are potentially taking breaks but no logging them meaning we are potentially over paying for hours that have not been worked.

Being able to review this at an organisational level would also be required to spot themes/trends and compliance

Example

  • 2000 hours worked in a week
  • 10 hours of breaks
  • Would identify that breaks are either not being taken or are not be recorded on T&A

Thanks

Graeme

PizzaExpress

posts.title: Add Field for Menu Selling Price (Inclusive of VAT) in Recipe Creation Interface
posts.details:
Currently, the recipe creation interface in Adaco only allows entry of the Net Selling Price (excluding VAT), which then supports cost percentage calculations. However, many operations, particularly in VAT-inclusive pricing environments, set prices based on the Menu Selling Price inclusive of VAT.

We would like to request the addition of a new field or configuration option that allows users to input the Menu Selling Price (inclusive of VAT) directly within the recipe interface. The system should then:

  • Automatically calculate the Net Selling Price (excluding VAT) based on the configured VAT rate.

  • Use the Net Selling Price to calculate the cost percentage.

  • Optionally display both values for transparency.

  • Add a toggle/checkbox to switch between net and gross selling price input.

posts.title: Carbon Labelling on (RME) StarChef
posts.details:
As a contract caterer, we aim to provide our customers with numerous delicious choices. While we don’t intend to remove ingredients that are associated with higher carbon values, we want to encourage our customers to make an educated choice and choose options that are less damaging to the environment.

There is evidence of a positive link between environmental knowledge and pro-environmental behaviours. So the more information we can provide to our customers, the higher the likelihood is that they will make an environmentally conscious decision and help us to reduce our carbon footprint. A study by Tjernstrom and Tietenbery (2008) showed that there are a number of different demographic factors that influence an individuals attitude towards climate change action. The study showed that individuals with an insufficient knowledge of climate change and older individuals were less likely to be concerned about environmental issues, which may be due to a likelihood that they will not witness the negative consequences of it. It is in fact younger and future generations who are the most likely to be concerned about the environment. Therefore, is it essential that we are able to provide knowledge to our customers at present and into the future, as it is likely knowledge of environmental impacts will become increasingly important to our customers.

There are certain ingredients that we know for a fact have an association with higher carbon emissions, however, it is difficult for us to quantify the carbon content of a dish, and to be able to provide our customers with the most accurate information possible in order to make an environmentally conscious decision.

The Power of Data

We are investigating carbon values for our entire catalogue of products and we would like to use this data in order to provide a carbon value for each dish using Star Chef. This way, a carbon value can be provided for a dish that is proportionate to the amount of each ingredient in the dish.

Legislation and the Competitor Market

A number of our competitors have already begun the process of carbon labelling in response to client interest….

Labelling of food with a carbon value may be mandatory at some point in the future, as some UK MP’s have introduced private member’s bills this year aiming to mandate environmental impact labels on food.
posts.author: Ian Smith

comments.author: Michael Hordern
comments.body:
Hi Ian,

A hot topic, indeed! :/

It's an area that I've been thinking about for a while. The ability to use the available data to calculate menu-, location- and company-specific CO2e footprints - and track the improvement of these over time - seems like something of genuine value (even without legislation).

Challenges

However, my research into what might be involved has led me to believe that this is a highly specialised area with a number of, as yet, unresolved challenges:

  • Where does the Life Cycle Analysis or Assessment (LCA) data come from?  This is a complex, specialist and country-specific process. There are a number of food-product LCA providers in this market using region-specific LCI data, combined with a proprietary weighting and rating scheme, to derive a single "score" or indicator for each of the customer's products. This indicator has the dual objective of informing consumers and of being an assessment and improvement tool for customers, manufacturers and distributors.

    These LCA providers, and their data and systems, will be an essential part of any solution.

  • What standards will apply? At this time, there are no agreed global or UK-national standards for how life cycle analysis - for food products - should be carried out nor on how this data should be reported to consumers.

    Indeed, Professor Robin May, the Chief Scientific Advisor to the UK’s Food Standards Agency (FSA) said on November 5, 2021
“Currently, there are no internationally agreed standards for eco-labelling, or for what type of data should be measured. This must be addressed urgently through collaboration between business, academia and government, so that the food system can be set on a path to sustainability.” https://www.food.gov.uk/news-alerts/news/urgent-progress-needed-on-a-unified-eco-labelling-system-for-food-in-the-uk

 

  • And which metrics to report?  The most prevalent metric across providers seems to be "kg CO2 equivalent" or CO2e, which corresponds to the "Climate Change" indicator or the amount of modification of the global climate (largely due to the burning of fossil fuels) caused by the product, reported in relation to the warming potential of 1 kg of carbon dioxide. 

    However, the European Commission has proposed the Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) and Organisation Environmental Footprint (EF) scheme, which suggests a much longer list of 14 impact categories including Ozone layer depletion, Photochemical ozone formation ("smog"), Terrestrial and fresh water acidification ("acid rain"), Particles, Land use, Depletion of water resources, etc.

    A single “EF score” is also recommended by the European Commission, calculated with weighting factors for each of the indicators; the weighting takes into account both the relative robustness of each of these indicators and the environmental issues. 

So, the correct determination and management of LCA and LCI data is highly specialised and complex and well beyond the scope of Fourth's interests. However, the intersection with ingredient and recipe data in the hospitality context and the growing interest in sustainability measures offer a clear opportunity to work with one or more partners to offer a valuable service to customers.

Possible Solutions

Your question hints at one possible approach: to implement a "nutrition-like" solution where, given CO2e values for each ingredient (imported from each customer's chosen LCA partner), Fourth could calculate (and re-calculate) CO2e value per serving of a recipe based on some simple rules. This is equivalent to current functionality for nutritional data, intolerances and ABV in Fourth systems and might include similar reporting and integration capabilities.

The alternative is an "outsourced" solution where, each customer's chosen LCA partner develops a facility to extract detailed menu/menu cycle, recipe and ingredient data from Fourth data (via existing APIs) into their own systems and all calculations of CO2e (and other future environmental indicator values, including a "score" or rating) per serving of a recipe, and all reporting and analysis, is done in that partner system.  One nice extension of this might be to return the partner-calculated recipe-level values to Fourth systems for storage and onward transmission to down-stream systems via existing integrations.

Of course, there are implicit assumptions in, and obvious advantages and disadvantages to, both of these approaches.

Right now it is difficult to predict how many customers will pursue this requirement, and how deep and wide the scope of those requirements might be; which partners customers may pick, and how their particular implementations will look; and what legislative and other considerations may emerge in, say, the next 12 months. 

Therefore my personal feeling is, that Fourth should look to pursue the "outsourced" model only, for the time being at least, but continue to work with customers and partners in this area and observe how things unfold.

 

It would be great to hear back from you Ian and of course from others in the Community - RME and Adaco users alike - what their experience, views and plans are in this area....

comments.author: Jon Thorpe
comments.body:
Hi Both - I'd like to throw Marston's interest into this conversation - we've all seen the potential for a relatively simple method to result in a dish calculation as per nutrition but its the measures against ingredient that pose the challenge due to the aforementioned lack of standards, both national and international.

If we collectively take a lead on this we could help direct the standard when the inevitable industry consultations start.

For now is it as simple as designing new measures (multiple) against an ingredient and the process to summate that measure to dish level with exposure of these values on the API channels?  Then when the sector has moved on further fourth will be ready with an environment that can start warehousing this ingredient data and reporting by dish?

My only thought will be whether there will be a need to report impact via different models. I come to this conversation as a novice but where does the CO2e or equiv start?  Food transport, food production, food preparation.  Along that supply chain from field to plate which businesses report which.  Will there be subsidies or motivators in place to pass your CO2e "responsibility" up or down the chain which must then be reflected in reporting.

comments.author: Michael Hordern
comments.body:
Hi Jon,

Thanks for joining the conversation.

When I started looking at this, my initial thinking was very much aligned with what you've said: surely this is relatively easily done if we treat CO2e as (more or less) another nutrient?  An extra field on the ingredient and the recipe, leverage the existing calculation and re-calculation triggers to sum the weighted values every time a recipe or ingredient is modified, and modify the import and export API to match, maybe even provide a new report or two.  I still believe that is a valid solution, as far as it goes.

However, I can also see a few challenges:

  • How do folks get the CO2e data in against their ingredients?  And how to they keep it up-to-date? Some (like yourselves) could probably use, or have their third-party LCA provider use, the modified import API to easily push in the data - exactly like nutrition today. 

    However, others may struggle with this approach and might prefer a solution more like we have for linking ingredients to a public nutrition data source such as McCance & Widowson in the UK.  We'd have to build that infrastructure and potentially cope with multiple different ways in which LCA providers might present their data.  That sounds expensive.

    If a third-party LCA provider managed the calculation externally then there would be the opposite problem: the customer would need to use their system would need to import and match Fourth's exported ingredients to their generic products.  However, there would be advantages: if rating schemes/indicators vary widely between customer-selected LCA partners and over time then this complexity would also be much easier to manage.

  • Is a simple sum of values correct?  From what I've read and talking to people it probably is for CO2e but that's because currently there isn't a better way.  The assumption is that all (most?) of the emissions are back in the supply chain (as you say) and so the way in which the ingredients are handled and stored in the kitchen or how the dish is cooked or how the waste is disposed of aren't significant contributors.  That assumption might be wrong, or might change in the future, and so the simple sum might not be enough....

    If a third-party LCA provider managed the calculation externally then they might have a better chance of adjusting their models to cope with this sort of thing.  And also with the inclusion of other environmental impact values like land use, depletion of water resources, threat to Orang-utans, etc.

  • Is there a requirement to dynamically "model" recipes for CO2e in an equivalent to lowering fat content of a dish?  One advantage to our current approach to nutrition is that the chef can swap ingredients in and out and get near-real-time recalculation of the revised nutritional values.  I don't see CO2e (and other scores) being used in this way, at least not now.  The "nutritional" solution seems like overkill.

    If nothing else the data isn't good enough.  One supplier's cherry tomatoes have exactly the same CO2e value as another's (from the same country, etc.) and so there's not a lot of modelling to do.  More likely this exercise is going to be about taking and comparing snapshots: "our new winter menu has 5% less CO2e than the equivalent menu from last year".  This approach is exactly what the LCA providers I've talked to are set up to do.

And I'm sure there's more we could come up with.

That's why, at least for the moment, my preferred approach is much simpler.  To have Fourth own the recipes and ingredients (as now) and expose them via the API.  Then let these emerging LCA providers own the CO2e (and other) data, own the calculations, and own the analysis, improvement and consultancy arising from that data. If they can also report the values back to Fourth at a recipe-level then that would be a nice bonus.

The CO2 tracking was initially implemented in RME which is our Recipe and menu engineering product utilised mostly by restaurants and contract caterers simply because at the time the demand for CO2 tracking was significant whereas the demand for the equivalent functionality in our hotel product (Adaco) was, at the time, little to none. 2. Working with the Zero Carbon Forum - We work with the Zero Carbon Forum and can provide them with an automated feed of a customer's recipes and ingredients from which they calculate the CO2 scores / footprint.  As this is a hospitality specific organisation many of our customers are members and use this method for their CO2 tracking.

Hopefully one if the above options will help you with your CO2 tracking and we will be sure to update you as and when we add anything to Adaco.

comments.author: Michael Hordern
comments.body:

Thanks for the idea.

Based on our analysis of the regulations and recent FSA guidance, we believe that RME (and Adaco) already provides the necessary data collection, calculation, and export (via the API) features required for the Calorie Labelling (Out of Home Sector) (England) Regulations 2021 coming into force in April.

We don’t currently provide any customers with facilities to print consumer-facing menus (or shelf-edge labelling) from RME and we believe that most use third-parties or in-house tools to convert the data we hold into public-facing documents.

We were therefore expecting people will want to continue producing menus in the same way they do today and simply take the calorie and portion size data from RME into that existing process.

However, if there are lots of users that physically type out menus (daily, weekly?) from RME (or Adaco) data then I can see that a report such as the one you describe might be useful.

I've marked this idea as open for voting so, if your users would also like to see a Calorie Labelling-specific report, then please vote and tell us more in the comments....

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for your message… and appreciate your observation on votes. 

We don’t have a minimum amount of votes required as each vote provides ‘support’ for the idea, not a threshold needed to enable development. Our product team are looking at all ideas for inspiration, and using the voting mechanism to understand our customer sentiment and support to help inform our next strategic developments to ensure we are developing with our customer’s views in mind. By all means, please continue to raise ideas! We are also actively encouraging more customers to engage with the ideas process by raising and supporting other customers’ ideas, which in turn should result in more votes being pitched on Ideas.

With regards to your specific request, whilst this is not a development planned in the immediate for the solution you currently use, we do have an entire PO approval workflow process in our Adaco solution. This solution is predominantly used in hotels and resorts where a PO approval operation is much more prevalent. You can see how that works here in our quick start guide to Adaco here and how to create an approval workflow in Adaco here. Whilst admittedly this is a different solution to the one you currently have, if approval workflows are paramount for your business, we’d be happy to discuss if Adaco is a more suitable solution for your organisation.

In the meantime, our Product Managers will continue to review ideas and consider how they may fit into our roadmap in the future. For reference, you’ll see any ideas marked PLANNED or COMPLETED. posts.title: Stock Period Length- Decouple Stock Period Approval from GRN export

Hello, 

Please may I request the decoupling of the GRN export to TS from stock period approval. 

Currently, on approval of the stock period (which is weekly) any approved GRNs are sent to TS for invoice matching. Please can the export of these GRNs be allowed without the needs for the stock period to be approved. Ideally, once the GRN is approved, it can be "locked" and exported (on schedule or on demand) For satiny purposes, please can a GRN export also be triggered for any approved GRNs, on the approval of stock period for any GRNs that were not already exported. 

Totally get that the GRN once exported cannot be reopened, and that's as it should be.

The benefit of this is to allow sites to move from weekly to monthly counts without jeopardising the 30 day supplier agreements. 

Thanks

Carol

posts.title: Stock Recon- Ability to filter the stock recon before running the report
posts.details:
Wagamama have recently moved to inventory from fnb and although there is resounding benefit to counting, sites have said running the recon is actually taking a but longer. Feedback has been that they would like a filter on the recon page, similar to fnb to exclude items below/above a certain value. e.g. £3.  I know the recon can filter on screen highest to lowest per category but the problem is once this is exported, the export forgets the filter and so sites have to edit the excel manually. They do use the excel when checking which items need a recount on a monday. 

So, can there either be a filter added to recon page when it's run and for that to remember on export page OR can the highest to lowest filter already there be remembered when running the excel or even better, is there a way to "tag" items from the recon for recounting on the counting app so users know which items need recounting please?

 

Thanks,

 

Carol

posts.title: Assign Multiple Outlets to One PR
posts.details:
As there been any conversation on developing a way to create one purchase requisition and be able to assign multiple outlets? (one outlets by line item or multiple outlets for one line item per PR)

Similar to the PO Center that has a box for Single Outlet, if we create a PR and check a box with Multiple Outlets, then we can add a product line and be able to select an outlet and account by line item.

We have scenarios that a PR needs to be allocated to multiple departments (services and contracts) and need to be able to just create one PR and split the expense/invoice between different cost centers.

I know about the “invoice Entry-Multiple PO/Invoice functionality but this is not an efficient process. We don’t want to create multiple PRs or POs for this process.
posts.author: Alfredo Vazquez
posts.organization: Loews Hotels Services Company, LLC (Fourth USA)

comments.author: Elaine Reilly
comments.body:
Hi Alfredo - as an alternative there is an option to merge requisitions into one PO.

in requisitions > process > purchasing requisitions

tick all requisitions to process then continue as normal.  this then merges into one PO ( or more depending on how many vendors are used)

comments.author: Chris Webb
comments.body: Yes as Elaine mentions the best solution would be to create multiple PRs, one for each outlet and then merge them into a single PO.  One of the challenges of having more than one outlet in a PR would be the approval process as PRs sre typically routed to different people depending on which outlet they are from.  For example the head chef approves PRs from the kitchen whereas the bar manager approves PRs from the beverage outlets

comments.author: Alfredo Vazquez
comments.organization: Loews Hotels Services Company, LLC (Fourth USA)

Thank you, Chris & Elaine.

Yes the timing of the approval process is an issue but we're trying to move "services" and "contracts" to Adaco PO and with this process we're attaching (back up) the quote or service or contract to the PR and the invoice will be coded to multiple cost centers. Some of these services are split between 4-6 departments. 

Our procurement process is centralized so we may have a buyer for multiple properties handling PO creation that did not automatically turn to a PO. We rely on req comments to know what vendor to turn the PO and the attachment. (using adhoc products) so we don't know if the requestor has created multiple requestions. 

This is why we were seeing if there is a possibility of creating one requisition and assign multiple outlets during the PR creation process. We need to push this process to the requestor and not the buyer figuring out which PR to select and combine.

posts.details:

Sales through our till system are marked as 0, while sales via 'Recipe Sales' are marked as 1.

We'd like user IDs displayed next to any depletions made through 'Recipe Sales'. The user IDs should relate to who posted the Recipe Sale on Fourth.

Countless individuals across our business have access to our Fourth system. We ideally need a way to track who is posting specific billed sales.

posts.title: Inactive products in RECIPE, on ADACO
posts.details:
Dear all,

We have noticed that when a recipe contains an inactive article, it does not display any warning or alert (such as an attention icon or message). As a result, users may not be aware that the article is inactive. (It's only when opening the recipe that we can see the product's unit is highlighted in red, and that no other unit is available — indicating that the product is inactive.)

My idea is to create a report or feature in the system that identifies recipes containing one or more inactive items, with the goal of either replacing those inactive products with active alternatives or deactivating the recipe if no suitable replacement is available.

Thank you.

posts.title: RME: Export API - Override Price
posts.details:
Hi,

We use the Override Price field (set within Price Bands) to override prices feeding into Tradesimple. This works well, and I can see from the catalogue feed file that the cost price in the Cost Price field is replaced with override price where override price is not blank.

However, this same logic (replacing the cost price with override price) is not applied to the Export API. Why is this? And could this be reviewed please?

We need the override prices to feed into Aztec Product Modelling via the ZDTS.

At risk of disrupting over customers' interfaces, and as the next best alternative, could you please add the Override Price field to the Export API?

 

Many thanks,

Scott @ Stonegate Group

comments.author: Leslie Grogan
comments.body:
Hi Scott

In case it's useful, there is an existing export API that includes override prices.

These are the properties in the response (with sample values):

"StarChefKey": 0,
"ProductGUID": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
"SupplierName": "Dairy",
"SupplierCode": "B365",
"PriceBandName": "Default",
"OverridePrice": "12.14",
"SupplierAccountCode": "21323"

Access to this endpoint requires a user name and password that are provided by Fourth's Support team.

Here is the link to more information on our website for partners using the APIs:  https://developer.fourth.com/en-gb/docs/recipe-menu-engineering-import-api/reference#operation/Ingredient_GetAllIngredientsPriceBands

Best regards

Leslie

RME Product Owner

comments.author: Scott Owens
comments.body:
Thanks 391481585392

The ZDTS doesn't use this import (GET) API. Zonal would need to use the existing export API to create products on their system, then run this separate API in order to get the override prices.

I will discuss this option with Zonal but we would still like the above ideas (replacing cost price with override price like Tradesimple feed OR adding Override Price field to the true export API) to be considered please.

Many thanks,

Scott @ Stonegate Group

posts.title: Stock period- Alerts on closing of a stock period if sites enter "unusual" closing count and/or negative closing quantity
posts.details:
Hello! 

I have a request on the stock reconciliation if I may.

Currently as a user, when closing a stock period,  the system can alert the user to any pending transitions affecting the stock period as well as any missing sales or empty closing stock fields.Ideally, Please consider also adding an alert if users are closing with any  negative stock qty. This is usually only possible if sites have incorrect opening stocks, sales, purchases or wastage and have not entered a closing count. As some businesses do allow theoretical closing stocks to be captured, when this happens, it causes issues with weighted average cost of goods. Not allowing a site to approve with a negative closing qty avoids this happening.

Understand that this function would only be possible if users do not have the setting for counting everything enabled in site settings.

Secondly or instead of the above

Please consider adding an alert for any closing stock qty much higher or lower than the opening/sales/transfers would expect, potentially within a tolerated range. I'd suggest this range to be nothing less than zero and nothing more than what the site started with plus purchases and any transfers in. 

For example, a site opens with 10 apples buys 10 apples, wastes 2 apples and has sales of 5, the system can expect the site to close with no less than 0 and no more than 20 apples. Anything outside of this range should prompt an alert to force the user to check the closing quantity, deliveries, transfers, sales again before approving.

The benefit of this is that it would ensure users are in fact checking their stock recon but also that it will highlight quickly for them which lines are not making sense. 

For businesses with 100's of sites and with managers being under pressure to deliver so much more these days, anything that points them quickly in the direction of what is wrong is a huge time saving benefit.

posts.title: Update Deleted Holiday Alert
posts.details:
The Alert "Deleted Holiday" has two main issues. Firstly, the alert includes all changes to holidays, not just deleted, so it is both misnamed and misleading. The alert should be changed so that there is the option to include only deleted holidays or both deleted and modified in the alert produces. 

Secondly, the Deleted Holiday alert informs us of who made the change but not who the change applies to, so if a manager or the system modifies or deletes a holiday, the alert does not tell us which employee the change/deletion was made for, so we cannot then look at the relevant employee record. The idea is to include both the person/system making the change and who the change is for.

posts.title: Approvals Button in Purchase Requisition
posts.details:
Hi,

I have realised that a number of purchase requests are being creating but the users creating them forget allocate an approval route. Many a times this boils down to the perception that since the user would have clicked on the 'Save' button when creating the purchase request, it is assumed that the request has been sent. Also the approvals icon is on the opposite corner of the screen that makes it easy to miss since populating the items to request is done in the lower half of the screen.

I suggest that once the 'Save' button is clicked, a pop up window should show up asking the user if they want to send the request for approval with a 'Yes' or 'No' option. If 'Yes' is selected the 'Approvals' window should automatically open and the process done from there. If 'No' is selected, the purchase request is just saved as a draft for further use.

Kind regards,

Andre Cauchi

posts.title: Company Sick Pay (CSP) Pro Rata Automation
posts.details:
Currently, where a company offers enhanced company sick pay driven by length of service, customers are having to create multiple versions of a contract to accommodate part time employees. This is because the settings do not allow for auto-calculation and therefore pro rata of CSP days entitlement based on contracted hours.

In the hospitality industry where we have high numbers of flexible members of staff with minimum contracted hours per week entitlement this is not suitable.

The current settings on Fourth can cause non-compliance, over payment of CSP mainly driven by inefficient admin due to the volume of contract variations required and manual maintenance.

Similar to how holiday entitlement can be auto-calculated for part timers if FTE is entered, it would be great if the contract settings on Fourth could pull from the figure entered within the 'contracted hours' section of the Employment Details page so that CSP is auto-calculated and pro rata'd based on their contracted hours.

Thanks

Hi 397187146432 / 21442010624781

Just to let you know that this is now planned and we will be starting the development work shortly.  We will be adding the ability to map rates provided by vendors against the rates set up in Adaco so that when we receive an electronic invoice which contains rates from the vendor we will be able to match these against the rates set up in Adaco.  We can then either update the value of the rate based on the value in the e-invoice or add the rate to the receiving where it is not already present.

  2. EDI - Adaco point to point EDI
  3. cXML - invoices from punchout vendors
  4. Trade Simple - all other formats

I will update again once we have a release date.

posts.title: Add The Original Recipe Number Onto Automated Emails For Recipe Draft Approvals
posts.details:
Idea:

Currently, whenever a recipe draft is approved/rejected, an automated email is sent out to whoever submitted the draft for approval.

The automated email itself only lists the Draft number and the property it was approved at.

It would be a really helpful if the original recipe number that the draft number relates to also appeared on the automated email.

Why would this be helpful?

In our business, we sometimes need to know what recipe number an already approved draft related to.

Since draft numbers disappear once they're approved, there's isn't an easy way to retroactively find this information.

By adding this feature, we could look back on our old emails and see exactly what recipes older recipe drafts relate to, even after they've been approved.

Conclusion:

Multiple users across our business submit countless recipe drafts every day. Often times these users lose track of what recipe each approved draft they submitted related to, leading to a lot of confusion.

To me, this suggestion seems to be a relatively small idea that would make recipe approval significantly easier for everyone involved in the process.

posts.title: ABC Analysis Report
posts.details:
We suggest is incorporating an ABC analysis report, which will enable us to categorize and prioritize our top products and vendors. This analysis is highly valuable for effective stock control, supplier management, and expenditure monitoring.

We are seeking a report that delivers the following key information headers:

  • Item Code
  • No.-  I would include the classification number, as the top item and referred as number 1;
  • Description
  • Total Purchase Volume/Quantity over a defined period (e.g., last 6 or 12 months or more) – preferably not annual so that the users may have the flexibility to choose the date range required;
  • Unit Price – I believe that it should read Average Price;
  • Total Purchase Cost/Spend associated with each product over the same period;
  • % Percentage Contribution to Overall Volume or Spend that each product accounts for;
  • % Cumulative Percentage to facilitate classifying items into categories A, B, and C based on their contribution (e.g., top 20% of items constitute 80% of total spend);
  • Vendor Details linked to each product or purchase – so that the user can relate who the suppliers where;
  • ABC Class to classify the products.

The report would need to have the necessary filters for analysis:

  • Filtering Capabilities such as date range, product categories, or supplier filters to refine analysis as needed.

The goal of this report is to streamline the procurement focus, and to allocate inventory resources more effectively, and identify opportunities for cost savings and supplier negotiations.

posts.title: Welcome to Ideas - Click for Full Details
posts.details:
Welcome to Ideas

This is our area specifically designed for our customers to post any suggestions for changes to the Inventory Management solution. To help us review your suggestions, please follow the information areas below.  We’ve also created a short step-by-step process to make it easy to start suggesting!   

 

Creating an Idea

  • Select 'New Post' in the top right corner
  • Ensure 'Ideas: Inventory Management' is selected as the Topic underneath the details box

When entering details about your suggested idea in the 'Details' field, please be sure to include the following information:

  • Business Requirement (Why is this change needed? What challenge does it address?)
  • Suggested Changes (How can this address your Business Requirement? What benefit will it bring?)

Your Idea will then be reviewed by our team and will be marked as one of the following:

  • No Status –Your idea has been received! Our team are currently reviewing your Idea and will be in touch shortly. 
  • Open for Voting – Your Idea has been validated by our experts, get voting! The Product Decision team will periodically review the ideas and any ideas selected to progress further, will have more detail provided once available.
  • Planned- Congratulations! Your ideas was selected and will form part of our near-term development strategy.  A feature inspired by your idea is in the product pipeline
  • Answered - Your Idea is either functionality we already have available, or not something we can facilitate, and we’ll provide further information within the post.
  • Completed –Inspirational! Your Idea helped our teams design and release a new development.  It has now been published as a release, along with a copy of the release note in your original post.  Enjoy!   

We aim to provide an initial status update to all Ideas marked ‘no status’ within 5 working days.  From there it’s up to our community of voters to help our Product Teams determine what’s next!  Unfortunately, our team won’t be able to comment on each individual idea, and some ideas may not be taken forward but our Product team and community of customers are always reviewing your ideas to influence how Fourth can develop and evolve our products for the benefit of all of our customers.

Voting

If you see an existing Idea from another Fourth user that you think would also work well for your business, please ‘Vote’ on the idea so it can help inspire our Product Team.

Select the title of the post, and then select the upwards facing arrow to vote in favour of the suggested idea. You can vote for as many ideas you think are important!  Thanks for providing us some valuable feedback as to how we can evolve your Fourth Solution!

posts.title: Counting APP - logic to review
posts.details:
Hi

I think the logic of the counting app should be reviewed.

At the moment when counting from the app ( certain  ingredients in certain departments only) and syncing,  it will erase the count of other ingredients ( and/or other departments) inputted through inventory  in the same account.

Additionally this only happens with values different from zero. There so  if i entered zero , values will stay, if entered 0.01 or any other value it will erase

The counting app should only overwrite the input of the ingredient or batches synced  and leave the others untouched as per inventory.

this is for the below reasons

- if we only want to count specific ingredients than the app will be useless as it will erase all the other ingredients allowing the system to carry assumed stock levels

Especially if for operational reasons and certain categories it is more efficient the layout in inventory (remember that in the app you cannot sort in alphabetical order , you cannot see the value converted, counting items can easily get deleted by users etc etc).

I kindly ask to Fourth to review that logic as  there is not side effect on the change i am suggesting. Instead it will enhance the system being open to wider  customers methods

posts.title: Counting APP - reorder the list of items
posts.details:
Hi All

i think it would be very useful if could improve the counting app allowing users to re- organize the order of the items

At the moment you are forced to count in the same exact order they were originally added.

Obviously this work the first time you set it up, but if you re-organize your store and that order is not efficient anymore you have no option but delete everything and from scratch. This again every time you rearrange your store/area

 

MAny thanks
posts.author: Ivan Braun

comments.author: Andrew Barber
comments.body:
Hi Ivan,

Thanks for your idea.

On the point on being forced to count in the exact same order items were originally added, this is not the case. The Counting app automatically remembers the sequence that items are counted in from period to period.

For example, if in the first period the item count sequence was:

  1. Coca Cola
  2. Sprite
  3. Fanta

But in the second period the order in which item counts were applied was: Sprite, Fanta, Coca Cola, then the sequence is updated to become:

  1. Sprite
  2. Fanta
  3. Coca Cola

This can be observed by navigating out of the area and back in. Once the count is submitted and the period rolls over to the next the updated sequence is preserved and presented as the starting sequence in the next period - in this way shelf-to-sheet is maintained.

A couple of additional points:

  • If items are added to the area these will be added in a position after the last counted item
  • Where there is no count for an item "0" should be input for the item's position to be retained

I hope this helps.

 

Andrew Barber

Product Manager - Restaurant Inventory

comments.author: Ivan Braun
comments.body:
Hi Andrew

Thanks for reply but this is quite impractical compared to ability to manually rearrange the order.

As is, imagine the scenario where in a certain area i count

- sprite

- fanta 

- cola

Then i run my reconciliation, check and adjust the count of

- Sprite 

Accordingly to this logic sprite would go to the bottom as last counted?

Or imagine where several user adjusted the count( one user counting on sunday night, and a new user adjusting only few of them in the morning)

Which will be the order for the next count?

Many thanks

comments.author: Andrew Barber
comments.body:
Hi Ivan,

I'm certainly not discounting the idea to allow for explicit resequencing of items within areas, this is a valid suggestion, rather describing the currently supported approach to sequencing.

With regard to your questions:

  1. If an item already has a count value within an area for the period and the value is updated (not removed) the item will remain in its current position
  2. If another user updates the count for an already counted line, based on counts submitted by another user, the sequence remains per point 1

 

Andrew Barber

Product Manager - Restaurant Inventory

posts.title: Open Shifts visibility for multiple sites
posts.details:
With the growth of the 'Gig Economy', it would be good to be able to offer our own version of this, in order to attract a more flexible sector of the workforce, who want greater control over when and where they work. Key principles as follows:

  • Individuals would be hired as full employees of the organisation, on zero hours contracts
  • They would choose how many hours they worked each week by picking up shifts they wanted to work (potentially with no minimum requirement)
  • They would be set in the system as 'qualified' to work in certain roles across multiple locations
  • They would be able to view and accept open shifts for all of (but only) the locations and roles they are qualified in
  • Rules in place to prevent them from seeing / accepting overlapping shifts, exceeding a maximum amount of hours per week, etc.

posts.title: Clock reactive to worst case
posts.details:
Scenario 1 We have staff who work split shift, at present the clock colour can only respond to one of the shifts.  It would be helpful if the clock could show worst case results, ie if the first shift matched T&A and the second shift has been missed the clock will be green, I feel this clock should be RED.   It does not highlight that there is T&A for the second shift but there is no shift - resulting in a staff member being underpaid

comments.author: Mark Garbacz
comments.body:
In the first half of CY2023, Fourth plans to improve the functionality of Open Shifts. This improvement will allow Open Shifts to be available to employees who are not employed at the shift's location. To achieve this, Open Shifts will be customized to be visible only to specific employees, based on their job role, brand/region. If an employee expresses interest in working at a location where they are not currently employed, the scheduling manager can use the my schedule app to create an employment for them. The first phase for this will be only support our UK HR & Payroll customers.
Please stay tuned for the release notes of this new functionality on Fourth Community.

A new scheduling user interface will be made available to clients for migration in the second half of CY2023. The updated scheduling version will now save employee ordering and sorting at the location level. This means employees will no longer revert back to the ordering of their primary location, and users can  re-order their employee list so that non-primary employees are located at the bottom of the schedule for ease of scheduling.

Regards

Fourth Product Team

posts.title: Adaco: Setting rate schedule and account on added lines if product is already in Guide
posts.details:

If a line is added onto an invoice (such as in the case of a substitute item), and that VPN identifies a product already in that outlet's Guide, the rate schedule and account assigned in the guide should automatically be picked up. Just further clarification on this:

We have a number of approved substitutions with our suppliers, complete with quoted & locked in pricing. These are full products in Adaco with relevant VPNs and are added to each Outlet's guide where appropriate.

posts.title: Holiday approvals by day - add 'tick all'?
posts.details:
Hello! 

I am passing on a suggestion from a number of our managers.

When approving holidays, we're aware that the requests can be displayed in days or duration. The system is pre-set to automatically display requests in individual days and depending on how a manager accesses the request (either directly through the employee or through the generic holidays tab), it takes extra clicks to switch to duration view. Even then, requests will sometimes be split into three or four durations due to non-working days. With the tickboxes also being quite small, they're easy to miss-click and often result in managers ticking, say 7 days, misclicking on the 8th and opening that particular day's request, having then go back to the list and starting again.

It seems that a 'tick all' box could resolve that issue - it has caused many frustrations so hopefully it's not too difficult to address? 

Thanks in advance for your consideration!

Angelika

posts.title: Request for Improved Log Out Functionality
posts.details:
We would like to raise a concern regarding the logout process for our Fourth accounts. Currently, the system does not automatically log out when we close the browser. While the "Sign Out" option is clearly labelled in the first window, the second window only displays a power button, which some staff members may not realise also serves as a logout option.

To address this, we have two suggestions:

  1. Ideally, the system should automatically log out the account when the browser is closed.
  2. If that is not feasible, we request adding a "Sign Out" label next to the power button, along with an arrow or indicator to guide staff on how to properly log out.

This feedback reflects input from colleagues who find it frustrating to log back in if they were not aware of the proper logout process. We appreciate your consideration of this request and look forward to your response.

posts.title: Display of Unavailability Requests
posts.details:
New Idea created from recent community post from 15778898727565.

--------------------
I’m following up on 26860422999181's request, as we initially raised this issue with her.

Please note that while all managers are involved in creating the rota, only the General Manager receives the unavailability requests and can approve them through the app. Assistant managers can only see these requests on the schedule after they’re approved, which means they can’t adjust shifts beforehand to make the schedule more effective.

We’re glad the system allows us to schedule shifts even when a day is marked as unavailable. Currently, employees understand that approved unavailability requests aren’t final until the rota is completed.

However, this means that once the rota is finalized, both the shift and the unavailability appear on the same day in the schedule, which looks unprofessional. We understand that only the employee can delete their unavailability request, but often they forget or don’t do it, even when they’ve agreed with the manager to come to work.

We would like to request either:

-an option for managers to delete unavailability requests after they’ve been approved,
or
-the possibility to show all unavailability requests in a list on the Fourth website (not just the app) before approval. This way, assistant managers can see the requests while creating the rota and approve or decline them as needed.

Please let us know if either of these options could be considered.
Thank you.

If no managers set up for a particular outlet, there would be one person always approving all invoices (typically accounting or general manager) that way the flow would still continue. 

This would all be taken care by the user admin, and the system would take care of the routing.

posts.title: Receiving App - Alternative Default Delivery Date?
posts.details:
Hi All,

Whilst using the receiving app we have noticed that if a delivery is not received using the app on the day of the actual delivery, if a user goes to try and accept yesterday's delivery today, the delivery date changes to today's date.

Whilst best practice would be to accept at the point of delivery, if for whatever reason this is not able to happen then we would expect the same behaviour as Inventory where the delivery date is static unless changed, instead of being dynamic and having to be amended back.

I understand the current logic, but it may be best to have this as a configurable option at a global level or even better at a site level if there are different brands within a company who may follow different practices.

Thanks


Rich
posts.author: Richard Hayden

comments.author: Paul Morris
comments.body:
I totally agree.

Whilst I agree with best practice and Receiving at the time of delivery this is not always possible, for example ...

- senior chefs may be busy elsewhere so a delivery might be checked in by a junior chef who does not have App access

- certain sites may have poor 4g/wifi signal in the kitchen therefore (as much as they would like to) they cannot Receive on the app immediately

In both instances, ideally these would be received on the app later that day, however this may not be possible until the following day which could default the delivery date to the following week and cause unintended stock discrepancies if not noticed and left unchanged.

comments.body:
I spoke with Carol and she clarified what she meant by this, please see below for her clarification. 

Thank you.

"I guess it's for various things. Ali

comments.author: Lia Villarreal Cruz
comments.body:
Dear 391566946751

Thanks for your getting back to us on this.

Please note that there is no specific legislation covering sabbaticals and therefore the CIPD guidelines are just a guideline, not a legal set of rules.

Furthermore, within their guidelines you can also find the following 

'During unpaid sabbatical leave the contract of employment often does NOT remain in force. However the employee's continuity of service may be preserved provided the employer and employee agree that this is the case' 

I have in the past checked this point with our legal advisors and they agreed that whether we decide to accrue holidays or not, depends on the agreement we reach with the employee as as mentioned above, there is no legislation covering this.

Could you please kindly review the idea? As mentioned before, this is becoming a more regular request and we want to be able to offer this to our employees without having to terminate them and re-starting them. 

Thanks,

Lia

posts.title: RME - Recipe Recalcs and Last Modified API Calls
posts.details:
When child recipes or child ingredients are updated for intolerances or nutrition the parent recipes get a last modified event from starchef admin as part of the recalculation.  This enables us to keep our data up to date in secondary systems by using last modified.  But cost price changes do not write an audit event even though the linked recipes recalculate.

This is the statement from the Chris who tested it:

“We found that when a recipe was changed via an F&R, manually edited or an ingredients allergen/nutrition information was updated then starchef does stamp the recipes affected with a last modified date that can be used.

 

However, if an ingredient has been updated for a price change this does not stamp and that is where Rob ran into a problems. As part of the process, the recipe cost is built based on the ingredients and their respective price for the UOMs located with the recipe, if there is no updated time stamp on the recipe then it is not pulled and recalculated so we encounter pricing drift hence why currently the job pulls all ingredients and then all recipes every morning currently.”

Because we can’t rely on last modified to show us cost price events our data we use for financial modelling drifts.  This means our current practice is to drop our tables everyday and rebuild every live product from the APIs which often results in timeouts and resource drain on all our systems.

Is there anything that can be done to create an audit event against a recipe if cost price calculations change?

Jon

posts.title: Leaver Statement of Hours & Pay
posts.details:
When leavers are processed in Fourth, they either retain access for 90 days, or in cases of termination are removed at once. In both cases, a former employee in need of their record of hours worked and pay received are not able to do so from the 91st day onwards, at the very most. Behavioural solutions (employees or HR administrators maintaining separate records) is a possibility, but in a digital era where information should be readily accessible at all times, this would be an unacceptable solution.

I propose instead that in the case of all leavers, a Leaver Statement ought to be generated, breaking down each pay period and detailing hours worked and pay received. This would apply to both wage and salary pay bases, and would be relayed to both the employee's personal email address and retained on Fourth for HR access. It would allow terminated employees to access data to which they have every right, and help all leavers to manage the details of their employment without the need for them to maintain separate records, an unnecessary expenditure of time on the part of the employee that could be readily provided automatically by Fourth.
