posts.title: Trade Simple- Check Quantity Seperate to Price on Invoice V GRN
posts.details:
Hello! 

I have a request from the finance team please. 

My understanding is:

Trade Simple checks the invoice totals (qty plus price) versus approved delivery totals (qty plus price) for the whole document, using a £ or % tolerance e.g. £7.50.

If the quantity does not match, but the overall value for that difference is blow the tolerance value e.g. I received 3 but was invoiced for 4 and the difference in value is less than £7.50,  then the invoice is sent for payment. Correct?

Our Request Is

For the system to have an option to initially check quantity, e.g, I received qty 3 and the invoice says  qty 3 (tick) and then check price, delivery price is £10, invoice price is £16.34 ( tick) and only then send for payment. 

If the check is on the quantity first then any time a received qty does not match an invoice qty, the system will not release the invoice for payment, even if within the price tolerance.

This would allow the team to increase the tolerance value on price (due to the fluctuating market we now live in) without risking a massive variance on qty of goods received versus qty of goods invoiced.

I hope that makes sense.

Thanks,

Carol

posts.title: Multiple employment for salaried staff
posts.details:
We have several staff on salaried (weekly and monthly) employment who also work hours in their multiple employment role at a different rate. 

Example

Jane works 12 hours (contract) a week at £12 an hour.

She also works 9 hours (multiple employment) in another role at £9 an hour.

Currently, as overtime is enabled, when payroll is calculated, the multiple employment hours worked calculates the 9 hours at £12 an hour and not £9 per hour as expected.

This impacts all team members who are salaried with multiple employment because the system is calculating the multiple employment hours as overtime. 

We would request a change in the system to allow salaried team members to be paid overtime on their salaried rate when working extra hours at their salaried role and pay the multiple employment rate when working at their multiple employment role.

This impacts several team members in our business and adds complexity on the reconciliation before we can sign off payroll. 

This is very high priority for us.

Carol

I hope these ideas will be considered as I feel there is legs in this part of the app to help comms and action for restaurants

posts.title: Multiple Employment - Costs Visibility at hourrs scheduled level
posts.details:
In our business we have employees working across multiple sites and in their secondary or tertiary sites they can be working anything from a full day (7.5 or 8 hr depending on brand) plus overtime down to 1-2 hours. 

Scheduling these colleagues across the sites will give us the correct data to post to our financial systems. 

However the costs shown in store are at either full day or half day level and as this is what the store managers see it is not possible for them to be clear if they are over budget during the week.  The salaries borrowed or lent numbers they see will not be correct.

Can this be amended so it correctly shows the salary costs beimng moved across the stores.
posts.author: Doug O'Connor

comments.author: Fourth Customer Success Portal
comments.body:
Hi 15210686004877,

Best wishes,
Fourth Communities Team

comments.author: Alison Barlow
comments.body:
Hi 15210686004877

I'm pleased to let you know that we have released a change to the wage cost calculation that will accurately provide costs when salaried employees are scheduled across locations.  Here are the details.

We are also looking at increasing the scope to cover multiple employments across divisions in the second quarter of this year.  Please keep an eye out for further release notes once this work is complete - which I'm hoping will be in the summer, 2026.

Kind Regards

Ali

posts.title: Add new employee record
posts.details:
Hi team,

Is it possible to add a new field to an employee record on Fourth?
Each year we have to do the Northern Ireland Equality Commission Report and it’s a huge admin task.
If we were able to add 1 or 2 new fields to the employee records for Belfast it would save so much time.
We’d need ‘Community Group’ (Protestant, Catholic, Neither) and possibly ‘Job Code’ with options 1-9.

Many thanks,

420202835332
posts.author: Katie Nutter

comments.author: Sam McNeil
comments.body:
Good afternoon 420202835332, 391566916951,

Thank you for raising this idea. 

I can certainly see how this would benefit those with employees in Northern Ireland, simplifying the approach to completing the NI Equality Commission Report. On that basis, I have opened up this idea for voting.

In the meantime however, whilst we don't have something immediately available for "Job Code", you could make use of the "Sensitive Information" functionality (if not already), where under religion there are two selections made available for recognising those of Protestant or Catholic religion employed in Northern Ireland:

  • Protestant (R)
  • Catholic (R)

More information is available here: https://help.hotschedules.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055617651-WFM-UK-UI-Refresh-HR-Recording-Sensitive-Information 

Thank you,
Sam McNeil
UK HR & Payroll - Product Owner

posts.title: EDI Matching Success Rate
posts.details:
We are looking for a report that provides the EDI matching success rate for those currently assigned to EDI invoicing. While we continue to add EDI invoice feeds, we need to determine whether this process is delivering measurable value to the AP team.

Specifically, we would like to understand:

  • Benchmark data showing if POs/receiving were auto-matched with the EDI invoice during initial receiving, after receiving, or if matching was completed by the AP team under Receiving Correction.
  • Whether AP had to manually “touch” the received PO to apply the invoice.
  • Common reasons for EDI errors.
  • Number of EDI invoice feeds that failed to auto-match due to rate, pricing, or receiving errors.
  • Total EDI invoices processed, error counts, and overall success percentage.
  • Percentage of receiving transactions that were ”Matched” vs. “Not Matched” with the EDI invoice during receiving.
  • Number of POs received but not invoiced.
  • For a given date range, the percentage of receiving that AP had to match manually compared to EDI auto-match.
  • Manual invoice rate percentage.

There are many variables when adding a supplier with EDI invoice feed, and this analysis will help us determine if the process adds value.

posts.title: WFM | Payroll | Cross Charging on Payroll
posts.details:
In our business we use Fourth Multiple Employment (ME) functionality, our employees are salaried and can earn overtime.  After all schedules are submitted and we run payroll we run the cross charge journal so the finance teams can apportion the costs to the appropriate locations.

The values we see in the cross charging journals do not work for us as a business.  We have confirmed with support that this is not a defect so we are raising this idea to allow us to be able to select an option to use a different calculation for the cross charging journal.  Assuming the current calculation is satisfactory for other customers using the functionality, and they will not want it changed. 

Here is an example of the issue we are seeing:

Colleague Jane Doe is based in Store A Store and is on a 7.50 hr per week contract.  In this example overtime is paid at the standard rate.  In a given week she may also work in Store B

In Week 41 she works 

  8.00 hr in Store A (contracted hours + 0.5 hr)

30.25 hr in Store B (overtime 30.25 hr)

—--------

40.25 hr Total

In Fourth the Journal will charge

  7.50  hr to Store A (base contract)

  8.00  hr to Store A (overtime where we would expect to have seen 0.5Hr)

22.75  hr to Store B (overtime, we expect to see 30.25 Hr, but contracted hours have been netted off)

Overall Store A is charged 15.50 hr and store B is charged 22.75 hr.

So Store A is charged for 8 Hr more than it used while Store B is charged for 7.5 Hr less than it used.

The idea we want considered is an optional configuration where in this type of scenario the journal charges the actual hours worked to each location, whilst not removing the current option for other customers who do not have issues with the current calculations.

posts.title: Welcome to Ideas - Click for Full Details
posts.details:
Welcome to Ideas

This is our area specifically designed for our customers to post any suggestions for changes to the Workforce Management UK solution. To help us review your suggestions, please follow the information areas below.  We’ve also created a short step-by-step process to make it easy to start suggesting!   

 

Creating an Idea

  • Select 'New Post' in the top right corner
  • Ensure 'Ideas: WFM UK' is selected as the Topic underneath the details box

When entering details about your suggested idea in the 'Details' field, please be sure to include the following information:

  • Business Requirement (Why is this change needed? What challenge does it address?)
  • Suggested Changes (How can this address your Business Requirement? What benefit will it bring?)

Your Idea will then be reviewed by our team and will be marked as one of the following:

  • No Status –Your idea has been received! Our team are currently reviewing your Idea and will be in touch shortly. 
  • Open for Voting – Your Idea has been validated by our experts, get voting! The Product Decision team will periodically review the ideas and any ideas selected to progress further, will have more detail provided once available.
  • Planned- Congratulations! Your ideas was selected and will form part of our near-term development strategy.  A feature inspired by your idea is in the product pipeline
  • Answered - Your Idea is either functionality we already have available, or not something we can facilitate, and we’ll provide further information within the post.
  • Completed –Inspirational! Your Idea helped our teams design and release a new development.  It has now been published as a release, along with a copy of the release note in your original post.  Enjoy!   

We aim to provide an initial status update to all Ideas marked ‘no status’ within 5 working days.  From there it’s up to our community of voters to help our Product Teams determine what’s next!  Unfortunately, our team won’t be able to comment on each individual idea, and some ideas may not be taken forward but our Product team and community of customers are always reviewing your ideas to influence how Fourth can develop and evolve our products for the benefit of all of our customers.

Voting

If you see an existing Idea from another Fourth user that you think would also work well for your business, please ‘Vote’ on the idea so it can help inspire our Product Team.

Select the title of the post, and then select the upwards facing arrow to vote in favour of the suggested idea. You can vote for as many ideas you think are important!  Thanks for providing us some valuable feedback as to how we can evolve your Fourth Solution!

posts.title: IDEA: Option for Universal Certification Expiration Dates
posts.details:
Please add the functionality to have Certification Expiration Dates update across all locations  for shared employees.  

  • Business Requirement (Why is this change needed? What challenge does it address?)   

Currently, we have to update Food Handler's and Alcohol Service expiration dates at all 5 locations for every employee.  This takes a lot of time and can lead to inconsistencies if the date is entered incorrectly at one location.

  • Suggested Changes (How can this address your Business Requirement? What benefit will it bring?)

Creating the option to set up certifications to be updated universally (like phone number, preferred name, and email addresses already are) it would save time and lessen mistakes.  By making this an option when setting up the certifications, organizations can have locations specific certification expiration  dates and/or company wide expiration dates.
posts.author: Julie Hiatt

comments.author: Chris Sundgren
comments.body:
Hi Julie, 

Thanks for the IDEA! We tentatively have this planned for Q4 of 2021.

comments.author: Julie Hiatt
comments.body: Great news!  I've been suggesting it periodically over the last 5 years.

comments.author: Julie Hiatt
comments.body:
Good afternoon,

Was this feature still set for Q4 2021?

comments.author: Chris Sundgren
comments.body:
Hi Julie! Happy New Year.

Here's the changes we are making to certifications. We expect to rollout the new cert features this quarter, most likely middle of the quarter. If you'd like to be a BETA for this and get early access, email me at chris.sundgren@fourth.com and let's talk and run through it live. 

  1. Ability to configure certifications at the ASC level. You can set the expiration rules or amend them as needed.
  2. Ability to require a certification for a job assignment, schedule assignment (current behavior) or a labor position (new functionality coming in Q2, 2022)
  3. Migrating current certifications to the ASC will be part of the rollout plan as will some logic if you change the cert expire rules (all in the ASC)
  4. Ability to group your certs from each individual restaurant/store in the ASC so you have one common certification
  5. We've already added (and released) a new expire type...Prevent from being scheduled. This allows the employee to remain active but prevents them from scheduled across any schedule assignment. Keeps engagement up so you can communicate through HotSchedules if needed.
  6. Certification ID was also added (and released). It's an optional field that can be used to store that employees actual certification ID for auditing

posts.title: Improve the efficiency of the Menu Cycle Publication Process (Sodexo)
posts.details:
The Issue

Each menu cycle deployment or publication run could involve multiple units having up to 20-30 menu cycles published

This involves single click unit selection per menu cycle, which could result in 2-3 full days completing publication requests

We are looking at ways of making this process more time & effort efficient

The Requirement

The ability to find a group of units which have had a selected menu cycle previously published to them, to select one, multiple or all of these identified units and to publish a new menu cycle to them

This would significantly reduce the time and effort spent on publication in addition to ensuring each unit had the correct content published consistently

For example, a seasonal limited time offer menu cycle may be published to 100 units which means 100 clicks to select the units. In 3 months time, the same units will require an updated seasonal limited time offer published to them.

As it stands, that’s another 100 clicks, or with this idea, maybe 5 clicks and complete

The Process

  • Search for all units receiving Menu Cycle A
  • Select one, multiple or all units
  • For the selected units, allocate the menu cycle you wish to publish
  • Click ok
  • Run verification check for selected units

posts.title: Run Menu Extract Report for multiple Menu Cycles at a Central Level (Sodexo)
posts.details:
The Issue

When publishing a number of menu cycles, the verification to location throws up multiple data exceptions on a unit by unit basis.

In absence of an Ingredient/SKU report via menu cycles, a Menu cycle menu extract report is run for each menu cycle to identify recipes in use in that menu cycle.

This is then used to complete multiple lookups against the BI Ingredient in use in recipes to get to the generic ingredient names in use in a menu cycle

From this, a lookup is completed against Spring Parent alternate report to identify all alternates (SKU’s) within a menu cycle

A further lookup is then completed from this to identify the status of each SKU within the Product Database to enable the appropriate corrections to occur

The ability to select one, multiple or all menu cycles for a menu extract report would reduce the hours spent, running, renaming, saving and appending the multiple menu extract reports required, as there may be up to 50 menu cycle menu extract reports required for a deployment piece of analysis

The Requirement 

The ability to select one, multiple or all menu cycles for a menu extract report would reduce the hours spent, running, renaming, saving and appending the multiple menu extract reports required, as there may be up to 50 menu cycle menu extract reports required for a deployment piece of analysis

Alternatively, the ability to run an Ingredient & SKU report for one, multiple or all menu cycles would suffice from a data correction viewpoint

The Process

  • Menu Cycle Reports (local and central)
  • Option to select one, multiple or all menu cycles
  • Option to select consistent criteria
  • Multiple or all selections to be appended into 1 excel document
  • Option to download report
  • Option to save report

comments.author: Leslie Grogan
comments.body:
Hi 115891343631

Thanks for the post.  

The 'group structure' in Recipe and Menu Engineering could be used to display a different collection of recipes to particular users (via their User Group and Group association). 

Each RME User Group is linked to only one RME Group.  Each Group has its own 'data sets' for Ingredients, Recipes and Menus.  If a 'limited recipe set' was created and attached to this Group, users who were linked to this group would see only the limited recipe set, not the full recipe set.

If you are not familiar with the 'group structure' and how it works in RME, please check the guides on The Community for more detail.

Best regards

Leslie

comments.author: Leslie Grogan

Hi Jessica

Thanks for taking time to suggest improvements to RME's Digital Recipe Cards.  There are a couple of small enhancements planned for this year.  In 2022 we would like to enhance the functionality further so we will be sure to consider your suggestions.

In case you have not found it yet, there is a way to filter by menu then search by recipe name.  

Here are the steps:

Log into RME

Select the Digital Recipe Card user group (if it isn't your default user group)

Select 'Add Filters'

Select 'In Menu(s)' > select required Menu from the drop down list

Add the recipe name keyword in the search box (top of screen, next to the magnifying glass)

Select the magnifying glass to trigger the search with both the menu and keyword criteria

When the search results are returned, they will match both the selected menu and keyword criteria

Best regards

Leslie

posts.title: RME - Changes to Live ingredients/Approval process
posts.details:
Morning. 

Would be amazing if you determine which fields you want to go through an approval process on a live recipe.

Example below based on how we work:

So we move recipes to live at the point we send costs over to finance to produce a margin model ready for a food sign off. Once sign of is completed, I then produce a product forecast for purchasing and at the same point nutritional and allergen data is being worked on. At this point the methods and photos haven't been completed. If not in a live status you are at risk of people changing costs/effecting margin & effecting forecast whilst relying on someone to tell you. 

Methods and photos are then uploaded however these changes are now being pushed through an approval process when the development chefs are ultimately responsible for spec's. This causing additional workload to multiple departments and would only need to go through an approval process if it was effect the margin the business would make or if it would be putting a customer at risk.

If you could choose which fields you wanted this would make such a difference. 

Ben

posts.title: Absence Analysis report
posts.details:
If I want to find out who was absent during a particular period (e.g. between 1 - 31 October) and enter these dates as the absence from/to dates in the standard Absence Analysis report, it only picks up people whose absence start date or absence end date (or both) fall within this period.

posts.title: Auto Expiry on Order Approval Tasks
posts.details:

Having discussed your idea with the Product Decision Team, it has been decided we will not be taking it forward as an enhancement to our Workforce management solution.

Information about the health of a person falls under the Special Category Data according to the General Data Protection Regulations and there are several considerations that should be made before storing any health related information electronically.

If you feel that the NHS selection of absence reasons is integral to the running of your company, you could create separate absence types within the HR Module (HR > Administration > Absence Types) that can be used with the different absence reasons. Here's an article that may help.

Kind Regards

Ali

comments.author: Leslie Grogan

Hi 404134101632

Your suggestion contains a valid idea for which other members of the Fourth Community should vote if they like it:  Inventory solution to support recipe ingredients with '0' cost price.

While '0' cost price ingredients are supported in Recipe and Menu Engineering (details below), recipe ingredients with '0' cost price are not currently supported in the Inventory solution.

As you mention in your post, the current process for Inventory customers is to define ingredients such as tap water with a low cost, e.g. £0.01 (1 pence) for 10 litres.

RME solution and '0' cost price ingredients

Fourth's Recipe and Menu Engineering (RME) solution allows '0' cost price ingredients.

In May 2021 we extended the support for '0' cost price ingredients to our Inventory solution.  Before we made this change, the 'site-linking validation' (during which data from Recipe and Menu Engineering is synchronised with Inventory) would not allow ingredients with zero cost to be synchronised with Inventory.  We changed the validation to allow this.

Here is a link to the relevant Release Note:  RME Release Note: May 2021: Ingredient List 'Ready for Use' Tick Box, Updated Recipe Reports, API Updates, Site-linking Validation – Fourth & HotSchedules Customer Success Portal

Best regards

Leslie

posts.title: Delta queries should include all changes which have been made to the record within the delta time period specified.
posts.details:
Short version: Delta queries should include all changes which have been made to the record within the delta time period specified, else it isn't a "true delta".

 


A longer explanation is available below, but appreciate this goes into specific detail so is much longer than a normal "idea". (Covers business case and issue with the current setup)

Support suggested I raise my issue here, so here goes:

I've built an integration to keep Active Directory accounts "in sync" with Fourth data. The idea being the entire workflow between HR and IT becomes automatic. (My business challenge)
I have an issue with "Termination Date" on HR accounts, and using the "Delta" toggle on the Fourth API Queries. (I'm pulling both the Employee & Employments queries)

Scenario:
User hands in their notice - HR update their record so that there is a leaver date set on the account. Integration picks this up (Delta query on Employment, Full query on Employee and merge into one set of results) and makes the AD account "match" so we can run the leavers process at that point.


User then rescinds their notice - HR update their record to remove the termination date. At this point, the API does not return that user within the delta, so that leave date is never removed by the integration.

Support have raised this with dev, but the answer came back as "working as intended" - which I disagree with, you should either be adding all changes to the delta (that's the point of the delta, surely?) or,
you should only put the changes within the delta query results, when they're going to be going "live"

 


I'm open to ideas or suggestions. I can give more detail on how the integration works if it helps.

Without the delta query working as intended, I have to perform logic vs each employee which is computationally more expensive, and obviously takes considerably longer (Comparing ~50 accounts during a small delta to thousands of a none-delta query.)

posts.title: Auto-calculate daily sales budget
posts.details:
Currently Secondary locations complete an internal PVR complete with SPPOR (Spend per pupil on roll) * roll numbers (which is split between secondary & sixth Form). This produces a daily sales Budget (Split by secondary & sixth form). Quantities planned by menu item are entered for the week ahead * Sell price, this produces a Production value. This Value compared to the total Daily Sales Budget gives the site visibility of whether they are over or under production target. This is then amended accordingly. Wastage is recorded on paper and entered into Saffron.

The following week, the site adjusts the same sheet based on the previous weeks outcome and can adjust based on production Vs wastage from the previous week. This means that as the menu is live across the term, the amendments required become less and less as the production numbers stabilize.

We would like to be able to enter the SPPOR Value and roll numbers into a menu cycle by day and by site and have the system calculate the Daily Sales Budget & COG’s by day, based on the logic above. Coupled with the sites planned quantities entered, the system can show how far off target the sites are with production Vs their daily sales budget. This will enable the site to manage their planned production and make adjustments accordingly, it will also help reduce wastage and ensure counter availability at all times.

posts.title: Free Stock GST
posts.details:
Hi,

We have been trying to manage our free of charge stock using method 2 on this guide Adaco: Managing Free of Charge Stock – Fourth & HotSchedules Customer Success Portal

However unfortunately this does not account for the GST that has been applied to the stock by the supplier. When you have received 12 bottles but the invoice is for 10 bottles @ $10 each there is a GST of 10% on the invoice and 10% on the product line. 

If you put 12 in the received column and 2 in the sponsorship column - adaco correctly calulates the cost of 10 items but is still reading the GST as 12 items and therefore the invoice cannot be posted against the order as the GST line does not match.

This looks to be a defect in the system
posts.author: Kate Sullivan

comments.author: Chris Webb
comments.body:
Hi 16407153041805

Thanks for you post.  We're actually addressing this issue so that the GST / VAT / Tax is calculated on the total extended cost for the line.  So for example if you have 12 bottles at $1 each and you have 2 sponsored the extended costs will be $10 and the tax will be calculated on that value rather than on the full $12

This should be included in our next release which is on 8th October.

posts.title: suggested ordering - better way of updating safety stock
posts.details:
Hi there, at PizzaExpress we are trialling suggested ordering. To give the managers comfort that it is ordering enough, we are setting a safety stock level.  I am having to manually work out what - say - two days' worth of theoretical stock usage is and enter it line by line, restaurant by restaurant into Master Data. This is beyond tedious. Also, as we are in the run up to Christmas, the mix has changed so that two days' stock of some lines has massively changed since I first did this in October. 

Could we have some way of setting safety stock to be, by default, X days' theoretical stock by supplier? For example, I would like to set fresh suppliers that come more frequently (eg Reynolds) to be 2 days' safety stock, and ambient/frozen suppliers that come less frequently (eg Best) to be 7 days' stock? I am imagining a box to enter the days of stock against the supplier, possibly in global settings. And then you could use the master data section to override this at a local level. It would only really need to update itself weekly, rather than every day. 

We don't want to give our managers access to Master Data and, even if we did, the interface to update safety stock is old and clunky.

posts.author: Georgina McCann

comments.author: Aneliya Bambova
comments.body:
Hello 402562165631,

Thank you for your request.

At the moment, we do not have a report that specifically extracts the data entered in the "notes" section of scheduled shifts into a reportable format by restaurant or by week. However, you can still access this information by printing the schedule that includes the shift notes.

To do this:

  1. Go to the Scheduling page.

  2. Click on View and choose Download Schedule PDF.

  3. From the Actions dropdown menu, select Display shift notes.

  4. Then click the Download PDF button.

This will generate a PDF version of the schedule that includes all the notes written by managers for each shift.
Best regards,

Aneliya

posts.title: Hard Restrictions for young workers - maximum working week in line with working time directive
posts.details:
Ability for organisations to put a hard restriction for workers under 18 in regards to maximum shift lengths, when hours can be worked eg past 10pm and maximum number of hours worked in a week

The current hard restrictions limit maximum hours in a day, however the WTD also sets out hard restrictions on maximum working weeks and breaks between working days which we would also like to set a hard restriction on. 

Therefore, we are requesting to extend the hard restriction to: 

-a limit of a maximum of 8 hours working time a day

- a limit of a maximum of 40 hours a week

- 12 hours uninterrupted rest between each working day

-48 hours (2 days) taken together uninterrupted weekly rest

posts.title: Ability to Restrict Multi-Employment Creation and Editing via Rotas Module
posts.details:
Currently, users with access to the Rotas module can create and edit multi-employment records even if restricted in HR. This gap in access control increases the risk of payroll inaccuracies and inconsistent employee records.

Suggested Changes:
Introduce a permission setting that allows administrators to restrict the creation and editing of multi-employment records via the Rotas module, independent of general rota access.

Benefits:

-  Aligns access control across HR and Rotas modules.

- Ensures correct job titles setup, which can impact Tronc payments.

- Prevents pay discrepancies

posts.title: Scheduling Module - Visibility & Actioning for Pending Unavailability Requests
posts.details:
The Problem: Currently, it is difficult for managers to identify pending unavailability requests within the Scheduling module if they haven't went into Team Requests in the MySchedule app. Without a clear notification, requests can be easily overlooked until they are manually checked.

Suggested Solutions:

Dashboard Alerts: Add a section to the Home Dashboard & Alerts page (perhaps by condensing the weather widget). A simple section showing: "You have pending unavailability requests", or if possible, similar to the HR Module’s holiday request notification would be ideal.

In-Schedule Indicators: Display pending requests directly on the Schedule page using a distinct "Pending" colour. Hovering over the entry could show an "Action Required" tooltip to make the manager aware they have to go approve/reject

Direct Action: Ideally create the functionality to approve or reject these requests directly from the Schedule view, eliminating the need to toggle between the Schedule and the MySchedule app.

comments.author: Chris Sundgren
comments.body:
Hi Victoria, 

This feature is not on our roadmap this year. As easy as it may seem, it is a hard problem to solve. Employees can be assigned multiple jobs and multiple schedules. When submitting a time off, they're not submitting it for just one specific job or schedule. Let's say you have a limit of 5 time off requests for your Server schedule and 3 for your Host Schedule. Johnny is assigned to both schedules and wants to submit a request off where there are already 5 approved requests for the same day/time for the SERVER but 0 request for the HOST. Since it is a future request, a schedule may not exist and the intention of the scheduling manager is unknown (will he be on the HOST schedule all week or a mix of HOST and SERVER). The same scenario would hold if we limited by JOB too.

Perhaps the solution is if at least one schedule assignment (held by the employee) has exceeded the allowable time off, then Johnny is prevented from submitting the request.

I'm curious your thoughts...feel free to respond back here. Perhaps others looking for this feature will weight in.

As a reminder, employees can see the number of requests that were already submitted when entering a time off so perhaps this would help if they know the policy limit you're wanting enforce.

posts.title: Idea - Gantt Chart style daily roster
posts.details:
The existing daily roster report displays the start and end time of each employee's shift. This is very helpful for our store managers but comes up short when the manager needs to have a snap shot of the staffing situation at any time. The Manager has to keep mental note as he/she goes down the list.

For example, if the Manager wants to know who is coming to work in the afternoon, he has to go through all the names and check their shift starting time. This is very complicated when we employ at some locations over 20 people every day across different shifts.

Currently in Asia, most QSR and retail businesses use a Gantt Chart style roster report where each employee's shift is more visually presented. This method easily presents the current planned roster at any time as well as presents a clear picture of the staff to come. 

I propose that we create a new report or modify the existing daily roster report to show employee shifts in this Gantt Chart method to provide better visibility and familiarization for Asia based customers.

posts.title: Email assigned on Requisition Final Approval
posts.details:
When a purchase requisition is final approved by the Dir of Finance, their email address is tagged on the email that is sent to the vendor. If the vendor selects "Reply" the DOF email will show and they are getting unnecessary requests that should be answered by a buyer/Procurement. 

Is there a way we can assign an email to when the vendor select "reply" this email will show instead of the Approver? 

I know there is an email that can be mapped under ADMIN-Communication From Address but this does not solve the issue. and it affects when routing the requisition for approval. instead of the requester's name, it will s how this email address mapped under ADMIN which it's not good.

please advise. Thanks.

posts.organization: Loews Hotels Services Company, LLC (Fourth USA)

comments.author: Asam Ali
comments.body:
Hi 397187146432,

Thanks for your suggestion! As you mentioned that Property > Administration > Communication > From Address is a workaround for this issue. Please can you clarify what you are referring to when you said email address mapped under admin?

Please feel free to raise a technical ticket if this functionality is not behaving as expected.

Thank you,

comments.author: Alfredo Vazquez
comments.organization: Loews Hotels Services Company, LLC (Fourth USA)
comments.body:
Hi Asam,

When we have an email mapped under the ADMIN - Communication and we route a purchase requisition for approval it will show this email address as the email sender instead of the requester. Same issue once the requisition is final approved, Notify PR Creator on PO Receipt and Notify PR Creator on PO Creation. These type of email notifications should still show the actual username instead of the email mapped under the Admin-Communication. The email/PO that is sent to the supplier should have the email mapped under the Admin-Communication. 

Another option is to be able to add a generic message on the body of the email to auto populate for all orders Auto Transmitted. This was mentioned on another Idea.

 

Thanks.

it would be great if Fourth would add an additional checkbox in ADMIN setting with "Use RQ requester email address when auto-creating and transmitting PO's after RQ Final Approvals". or if there would be a way to add an email address in settings that would do the same process....For Final Approval reqs only.

posts.title: We would like to be able to search the entire RME (StarChef) database for a product code
posts.details: Hi there, we sometimes have an ingredient on StarChef that has been moved into an archive set, or an old unused set, or even without a set at all - but it is using a code that we need to re-use in a live set. We only get the error message at the end of the creation process, and then we have to go hunting in each set, and there might be many of them, to find the offending item. If the ingredient is set-less that is even harder.  We would like for Admins to be able to search the entire database easily.
posts.author: Tina Plewes

comments.author: Thomas Allies
comments.body:
Hi Tina,
 
Good news! We already have this functionality available and ready for you to use.
 
You can utilise the 'Ingredient Sets' tab in RME/Starchef under admin to locate the ingredients located in the sets in your portal.
 
RME/Starchef > Admin > Select > Ingredient Sets
 
Using the path above you can see which ingredients are assigned to each of the sets.
 
Be sure to follow our Release Notes so that you can stay up to date with all the changes to your Fourth
solution.
 
I have left a link below which will lead you to an article you can look for on knowledge that shows how to follow release notes.
 
https://help.hotschedules.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047940772-Fourth-Processes-Following-Release-Notes#:~:text=See%20more-,Customer%20Success%20Portal%3A%20Following%20Release%20Notes,-Fourth%20Customer%20Success
 
Have a good week!
 
Tom

comments.author: Tina Plewes
comments.body: No, that's not we are after. We know we can see ingredients in 'Ingredient Sets' in admin.  But there is no search facility in the admin section, and besides we would like to be able to search *the entire database* in one go. And we would like to be able to find set-less ingredients, as it *is* possible for an ingredient to become set-less.

comments.author: Thomas Allies
comments.body:
Hi Tina,

You can achieve this by using Groups, Sets & User Groups.

You can create a group, that has all required sets linked to it (Live, Archive, and any others you might have).

A User Group can then be created and linked to your new group.

It is recommended that a User Group linked to a Group with a mix of sets like this be restricted to minimal users.

Here are some useful articles in relation to this:
https://help.hotschedules.com/hc/en-us/articles/360052783212-RME-Creating-Groups-in-Recipe-and-Menus
https://help.hotschedules.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056383811-RME-How-to-Amend-User-Groups

Kind regards,

Tom

comments.author: Tina Plewes
comments.body: Thank you Tom, I'll pass that onto our StarChef admin to see that's a suitable solution. It's a bit of a workaround, though, to be fair. It would be great if the admin section of StarChef had its own (database wide) search function.

posts.title: A new, easy-to-read, adjustable graph view in scheduling
posts.details:
In Rotas, there was always the option to look at a graph view of the day, which would show you every team member's shift plotted against the hours of the day. It was clunky, hidden, unclear and barely used by anyone.

It was, however, a very useful tool for busy pubs to see how many people were on at any one time throughout the day. It was not used much due to it's lack of clarity and the fact that few people knew where it was. 

I've been using a spreadsheet to create something similar but was expecting to see something like this in the new Scheduling and it seems like a missed opportunity. 

The shift could be created as it is currently in the normal view, but in the graph view it would show all of the shifts against each other and mean you could adjust start/finish/break times to ensure you had the right amount of people at each 15 or 30 minute interval and make better use of labour hours and ensure you had the most economical rota possible.

posts.title: RTW Checks (Outside of EU)
posts.details:
When carrying out RTW checks, we can use just a share code as proof of right to work.  When entering in Fourth, its fine for EU citizens under the settlement scheme, but are finding that with other nationalities, we don’t have an option to input the share code as proof.

For example, for Nigerian Nationalities, I have input an additional proof type as “Non EU Share Code”  but it doesn’t follow the same format as when inputting for an EU citizen.  Do you know how this can be fixed?  Share codes are now the standard for proof of RTW.
posts.author: Jack Worsley

comments.author: Jack Worsley
comments.body: 416120062332

comments.author: Alex Evans
comments.body:
Hi there, 
 
As share codes become more standardised for proving right to work, Fourth will be including new features on to the system. However, the only supported share code from within the create employee screen currently is the one associated to EU citizens as this was the first type of share code to be adapted by Fourth.
 
Hope this helps.

 

Regards, 

Alex

comments.author: Alison Barlow
comments.body:
Hi 391481415412 & 416120062332

It is possible for Nationalities to be assigned to the proof Of eligibility for Settled Status from HR Module > Administration > Proof of Eligibility > Select Settled Status > add Nationality

More information about how to manage the POE within your portal can be found here

As Alex mentioned above, in 2023, we will be enhancing the current POE section within the employment details page of an employee's record to make it more aligned with the current proof of eligibility rules.

Kind Regards

Ali

posts.title: Welcome to Ideas - Click for Full Details
posts.details:
Welcome to Ideas

This is our area specifically designed for our customers to post any suggestions for changes to the Mobile & Apps solution. To help us review your suggestions, please follow the information areas below.  We’ve also created a short step-by-step process to make it easy to start suggesting!   

Creating an Idea

  • Select 'New Post' in the top right corner
  • Ensure 'Ideas: Engage & WFM Mobile Apps' is selected as the Topic underneath the details box

When entering details about your suggested idea in the 'Details' field, please be sure to include the following information:

  • Business Requirement (Why is this change needed? What challenge does it address?)
  • Suggested Changes (How can this address your Business Requirement? What benefit will it bring?)

Your Idea will then be reviewed by our team and will be marked as one of the following:

  • No Status –Your idea has been received! Our team are currently reviewing your Idea and will be in touch shortly. 
  • Open for Voting – Your Idea has been validated by our experts, get voting! The Product Decision team will periodically review the ideas and any ideas selected to progress further, will have more detail provided once available.
  • Planned- Congratulations! Your ideas was selected and will form part of our near-term development strategy.  A feature inspired by your idea is in the product pipeline
  • Answered - Your Idea is either functionality we already have available, or not something we can facilitate, and we’ll provide further information within the post.
  • Completed –Inspirational! Your Idea helped our teams design and release a new development.  It has now been published as a release, along with a copy of the release note in your original post.  Enjoy!   

We aim to provide an initial status update to all Ideas marked ‘no status’ within 5 working days.  From there it’s up to our community of voters to help our Product Teams determine what’s next!  Unfortunately, our team won’t be able to comment on each individual idea, and some ideas may not be taken forward but our Product team and community of customers are always reviewing your ideas to influence how Fourth can develop and evolve our products for the benefit of all of our customers.

Voting

If you see an existing Idea from another Fourth user that you think would also work well for your business, please ‘Vote’ on the idea so it can help inspire our Product Team.

Select the title of the post, and then select the upwards facing arrow to vote in favour of the suggested idea. You can vote for as many ideas you think are important!  Thanks for providing us some valuable feedback as to how we can evolve your Fourth Solution!

posts.title: Booking Lieu days on App
posts.details:
It would be good to have a way that employees can book outstanding Lieu days on the App. As we are a 24/7 business we have a lot of employees who accrue lieu days for BH or working days off and then want to book them to create a long weekend off or add on as part of a holiday booking.  But there is no way to do this on the App. Only paid holidays or unpaid holidays for days off. 

We were just about to move over to using the APP for booking holiday but have now put a halt to it as we don't know how to get over this problem. If employees are booking flights they want confirmation that this time off is approved.

Does anyone else have a way of dealing with this?

Thanks

comments.author: Simon Montalvo
comments.body:
Hi Deborah,

Hope you are well.

This request was previously brought to our attention by several customers, which is why there is a Lieu day functionality release on the way which will enable Lieu days to be directly booked on to Scheduling.

There is no set date as to when this new functionality will be incorporated yet, however I would keep an eye out on the CSP for a release note regarding this new feature.

In the meantime we would recommend using a Lieu day shift type on Scheduling to mark when Lieu days are being taken (please note that this will not automatically set the Lieu Day as 'Taken' on HR as this will need to be done manually).

Simon Montalvo

comments.author: Saradhi Valluri
comments.body:
Hi, Remco Verhaaf.
 
Fourth Analytics can be used to see a KG/Ltr-based breakdown of purchases by supplier, category, and product. This report includes purchasing quantities and prices in KG/Ltr. (if defined in Adaco). For example, if you have defined a product in Adaco as 12 packs of 2 KG each, the report will show 48 KG and the KG price when you purchase 2 cases of the product. You can extract the data from the report in Fourth Analytics and calculate the rebate amount using your rebate percentage. Even if you define your product in Adaco in grams, it will convert to KG and provide the details in Fourth Analytics.
  • To see this report, in Fourth Analytics go to the 02. Cost Price Analysis dashboard
  • Then go to the YOY Price Movement tab and find the ADACO - YOY Base Price Variance by Vendor report
This should display your required data, as explained above. We hope this helps. Please let us know if you have any further questions.
 
Thanks

Fourth Communities Team

posts.title: Adaco: Allow trigger for recipe preparing outlet based on category
posts.details:
Good afternoon,

It would be amazingly beneficial for us if a trigger or option could be allowed to let us automatically assign recipe preparation outlet based on recipe category. Our sales mix is 100% recipe, and for 45 properties it's unfeasible for us to manually set preparing outlet on each recipe for each property. All of our property outlets are set up with the same structure.

Adding this feature would allow for us to automatically decrement products stored in the kitchen outlet for all food recipes when a wastage sale is recorded in our Food Wastage outlet. We can't use par levels because that would deduct more than what was used, since it will round it up to the nearest whole inventory unit. 

 

Thanks,

Tim
posts.author: Tim Welsh

comments.author: Tim Welsh
comments.body:
Just for added context, this is the workaround that we had to build because Adaco is currently unable to process wastage transactions from the POS even though wastage transactions are supported by the API for use in other packages.

This solution has eliminated a lot of the tedious double-handling that was occurring so that we could record all of our FOH wastage in addition to our BOH wastage.

Having an automatic trigger to set recipe preparation outlet based on recipe category (or assigned COGS account) would go a long way to reducing further admin time.

As this is an individual requirement for your business we can discuss this further on our call this week.

This mostly supported. When you review your scheduler, you will see a purple badge under an employee's name that's M (for minor). To enable visibility  of the badge in the Roster Report (from the Scheduler), you will need to configure Minor Rules in your Above Store Console. I setup one for Pennsylvania which is where the Drexell location is so you can see this in action.

In the scheduler, you can filter by attributes (so Minor in this case) and if you do hire 14-15 and 16-17 yr olds, you'll be able to filter by those age range definitions too. Given you're in some areas where there are restrictions for minors and there are requirements for meal and breaks, I highly recommend you configure these in your ASC. Currently you don't have access to do this but if you're an authorized approver, you can submit a help ticket to enable access to Minor Rules, Meal and Break Rules. I also recommend for your minor employees you setup school calendars (this is done at the site level by way the staff tab) as that directly influences when school is in session or when it's not in session (for summer break). Non session is defined as 3 or more consecutive weeks of no school in the calendar. Typically, you may need a calendar for each unique school or ISD where you employees go since spring break, first and last day of school can vary.

I also see you're in a few cities where Fair Work Week ordinances are applicable. We have a number of features here to help ensure you're compliant with those complex labor laws too.

I'll look at adding a filter to the Roster report so if you print, you can filter directly to that attribute. 

Here's some help links

https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/child-labor

https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/rest-periods

https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/meal-breaks

https://help.hotschedules.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001433512-HS-Setting-Up-School-Calendars

posts.details:

I don't believe it's currently possible for employees to use holiday entitlement to top-up their pay while off sick - please correct me if I'm wrong?

However, as per the ACAS article - https://www.acas.org.uk/checking-sick-pay/sick-pay-and-holiday-pay - employees can request for that to happen. Currently however, I have been advised that for a month long sickness, where employee has reached half-pay CSP entitlement, I should break the absence into two and enter half the month as sick leave, half as holiday (so the employee receives their usual monthly pay, at their request). This isn't a feasible solution as it will affect the SSP calculations, CSP entitlement will only be used up by half of what it should and obviously the Bradford Factor will also be affected. 

Unless I'm missing a workaround, it should be given serious consideration given that ACAS informs employees they can in fact request for this to be done.

Thanks

Angelika

posts.title: Irregular hour workers & "Casual" setting - Holidays
posts.details:
Please can you look into changing how and when the holidays update for "casual" employees. 

 

It seems bizarre, that holiday accrual only updates when schedules are submitted (so it's not in real time) and that employees cannot plan ahead and book holidays fore the future if they haven't earned the accrual yet. This causes unnecessary admin time for both HR (manually changing the "holiday allowance calculated" global setting, to add the holidays, then change the setting back) and the Managers a waste of time using spreadsheets to keep up with requests for successful planning. We're setting ourselves up for failure and forgetting staff requests! 

I'd like to propose you look into:

1. Holiday accruals for irregular workers under the "casual" setting update weekly, rather that when schedules are submitted
2. Irregular workers under the "casual" setting should be able to request unaccrued holiday

 

Thank you
posts.author: Gemma Buller

comments.author: Alison Barlow
comments.body:
Hi 12505374460813

Thank you for your suggestion.  The Casual Holiday accrual has been designed to accrue upon submission of the rota.  This is because, it is only once submitted, that a rota has been finalised and signed off as accurate.  Best practice within scheduling is to submit schedules on a weekly basis after the final shift of the week has been completed.  This way, not only will the casual holiday accrue, it will also mitigate risk of late or non submission when it comes to the payroll week, and also allow for accurate weekly reporting.

In regards to allowing employees to book holiday when it is not yet accrued, there are settings within the Job Titles that will allow this to happen.  To find job titles, go to HR > Administration > Job Titles, then find the required job title, use the drop down in the top right to select Edit Default Holiday.  The first group of settings relate to how employees are allowed to request holidays.

I hope this helps,

Kind Regards

Ali

comments.author: Sam McNeil
comments.body:
Good afternoon 1905664553327

Thank you for your suggestion and for engaging with the ideas portal.

We understand your need for Area Managers to support salary changes across multiple locations without being granted full access. However, the current system architecture is designed to preserve strict data access controls, particularly around sensitive information such as salary and employment details.

Allowing Salary Workflow access independently of broader HR/Payroll/Rota permissions would bypass these controls and expose information that Area Managers are not currently authorised to view. This would conflict with the system’s intended hierarchy and security model.

Additionally, with the upcoming release of the enhanced Employment Change Request feature (a rework of the existing Salary Request Workflow), even more employee information will be visible as part of the process, which further reinforces the need to restrict access appropriately.

At this time, we have not identified a viable way to achieve the requested functionality without compromising data privacy or system integrity. As such, we will not be progressing this idea further.

Thank you,
Sam McNeil

comments.author: Chris Sundgren
comments.body:
Hi Tyler, 

I looked at your meal break rules and just want to confirm intended configuration. Your meal rules configured in your ASC have two different rules within the set, a 4hr duration PAID 30 minute Break and a 6hr shift duration with a 30 minute paid Break. Is that intended? Typically for California the configuration looks like the image below (and if you do use Waivers, another rule in the set where the meal values are 6 and 12. The paid rest breaks are the same for Waiver and Non Waiver.

When you apply the times to a shift as you're doing, we'll put those meals and breaks in a way to ensure they're not taken beyond the required time. If you edit the placement of those meals and breaks, they will persist. I see you're copying schedules from one week to the next. In that copy modal window, there's a checkbox to "copy meal and break edits". Are you checking that flag?

It's by design to remove meal and breaks from the a shift if it's housed. This is because we don't know what team member is picking up nor their meal break policy assignment so it will recalculate the placement of any required meal or rest break based on their assigned policy once it's approved. 

An alternate configuration option is to NOT apply the times directly to the shift. When that flag is left unchecked, we'll still account that a meal or rest break is required and then on the daily roster from the scheduler, you can input time or even an order sequence of who should go on the meal or break first.

Individual Employee Notes – While the system allows managers to plan schedules in advance, we suggest adding a feature where managers can attach individual notes to each employee’s schedule, rather than applying notes to the entire department for the whole week. posts.title: SSP to be calculated based on contracted hours for wage cost
posts.details: When sick pay is added to fourth on it wage cost it reflects the full time flat rate of SSP even for part time people. Please can this be changed so the wage cost is relevant to the contracted hours.
posts.author: Sophie Baker

comments.author: Sam McNeil
comments.body:
Good afternoon 18076668267405

We appreciate your suggestion and understand the desire for a more accurate reflection of SSP wage costs, particularly for employees with different employment statuses. 

While SSP entitlement itself is a fixed weekly amount regardless of contracted hours, the actual calculation of SSP for payment purposes does still take into account an employee’s working pattern - specifically the number of qualifying days per week. In our system, whilst it calculates exactly in the payroll module, the SSP wage cost is calculated by dividing the standard weekly SSP rate by seven, providing a consistent daily rate across all employees.

We recognise, however, that this method may not always feel fully representative of the true cost for employees with fewer working days. While adjusting SSP wage cost calculations based directly on contracted hours would not align with statutory SSP rules, we do agree there could be benefits to offering a more nuanced costing model.

With that in mind, we are happy to put this idea forward for wider customer feedback and voting, so we can assess broader demand and prioritise any future enhancements accordingly.

Thank you,
Sam McNeil
Product Owner - UK HR & Payroll

posts.title: Annualised Hours + System Compatibility
posts.details:
Annualised Hours employees receive 1/12th of their annualised salary regardless of ‘actual’ hours worked in the pay period.  The business calculates the ‘cost’ to the business based on the actual hours worked by the employees.  Positive and negative hours for these employees are managed using the Fourth Lieu time functionality. In the current Fourth platform the ‘Rota Wage Cost’ displays the set salaried amounts which does not reflect the productive cost to the business.  In order to provide accurate operational costs this needs to be the hours scheduled multiplied by the employees hourly rate – rather than the employees summary.

Annualised hours employees also have an equivalent of guaranteed minimum annual hours for their casual workers.  These workers receive the same pro-rated holiday allowance (30 days FTE).  Due to system restrictions the global setting for casual holiday accrual rate cannot change by site location.  Functionality to be able to amend casual holiday percentage accrual rate by site level is therefore requested for review and development.

posts.title: Reporting on EDI Invoicing Matching Success Rate
posts.details:
As we continue to onboard more suppliers with EDI Invoicing integration, we would like to request the development of a reporting feature that provides visibility into the EDI matching success rate.

The goal is to evaluate whether the EDI Invoicing functionality is delivering the intended efficiencies through Auto Matching, or if manual intervention is still frequently required. For example, we’ve observed instances where a receiving does not auto-match due to discrepancies such as additional rates or mismatched amounts submitted by the supplier. In such cases, AP must manually adjust the receiving, which undermines the benefits of automation.

A report that highlights:

The percentage of EDI invoices that auto-match successfully,

The suppliers with the highest and lowest match rates,

Common reasons for failed matches (e.g., rate discrepancies, missing data),

...would be extremely valuable. This insight would help us determine whether expanding EDI Invoicing to additional suppliers is beneficial for both AP and the suppliers themselves.

Ultimately, if AP still needs to manually touch receivings due to frequent mismatches, the value of EDI integration is diminished. Having this data would allow us to make informed decisions and work with suppliers to improve data accuracy.

posts.title: Rolled Up Holiday Pay For Casuals to Calculate as per Government Examples
posts.details:
Caveat - We have not switched on the rolled up holiday pay for casuals functionality within Fourth, we have been investigating this as we would like to.

Our communications with Fourth suggest that the rolled up pay for casuals is calculated at 12.07% of HOURS worked in the week, rounded up to the next hour, paid out at the casual employees hourly rate. GOV.uk states that it should be paid out at 12.07% of TOTAL PAY for that week. These are two different calculations and lead to different results. 

This is based on the example give in hot schedule: April 1st 2024, Release Note: WFM UK | UK HR & Payroll: Casual Holiday for Part-Year and Irregular Workers – Fourth & HotSchedules Customer Success Portal and the example in 6.2 of Holiday pay and entitlement reforms from 1 January 2024 on Gov.uk.

The employee in the example in the hot schedule receives £75 for the first week for holiday pay, however if the GOV.uk guidance for calculating this is used, it would be £72.42 for that same week. Therefore, this leads to an overpayment of holiday. Whilst this might appear be a minimal difference for this singular employee, over many casual employees and an entire year, this will mount up. 

I propose that the Government guidance for calculating rolled up holiday pay for casuals is used instead of the current method.
posts.author: Allaina Watkins

comments.author: Sam McNeil
comments.body:
Good morning 414108687632

Thank you for your message and for raising this point.

I can confirm that the rolled-up holiday pay calculation within Fourth is compliant with the Government guidance. While our system expresses the calculation based on hours worked, it ultimately produces the same result as the 12.07% of total pay method outlined on GOV.UK.

For example:

Legislation:

  • 40 hours worked at £15 per hour, totalling £600.
  • £600 * 12.07% = £72.42

Fourth:

  • 40 hours worked * 12.07% = 4.828 hours
  • 4.828 * £15 hourly rate = £72.42
  • Only the payslip, this would be represented as 4.828 units at the £15.00 amount using the pay element "Rolled Up Holiday Pay".

The end result is identical, but represented differently.

That said, you are absolutely right that the example in the supporting article does not clearly reflect this and could be misleading. I’ll be updating that documentation to clarify the calculation and will let you know once the revised version has been published.

Thank you again for flagging this, it’s very helpful feedback.

Kind Regards,
Sam McNeil
Associate Product Manager

comments.author: Sam McNeil
comments.body:
Good morning 414108687632,

The following article has now been updated: 

  • April 1st 2024, Release Note: WFM UK | UK HR & Payroll: Casual Holiday for Part-Year and Irregular Workers

Thank you again for bringing this to my attention.

Thank you,

Welcome to Ideas

This is our area specifically designed for our customers to post any suggestions for changes to the WFM US | HotSchedules solution. To help us review your suggestions, please follow the information areas below.  We’ve also created a short step-by-step process to make it easy to start suggesting!   

 

Creating an Idea

  • Select 'New Post' in the top right corner
  • Ensure 'Ideas: WFM US | HotSchedules' is selected as the Topic underneath the details box

When entering details about your suggested idea in the 'Details' field, please be sure to include the following information:

  • Business Requirement (Why is this change needed? What challenge does it address?)
  • Suggested Changes (How can this address your Business Requirement? What benefit will it bring?)

Your Idea will then be reviewed by our team and will be marked as one of the following:

  • No Status –Your idea has been received! Our team are currently reviewing your Idea and will be in touch shortly. 
  • Open for Voting – Your Idea has been validated by our experts, get voting! The Product Decision team will periodically review the ideas and any ideas selected to progress further, will have more detail provided once available.
  • Planned- Congratulations! Your ideas was selected and will form part of our near-term development strategy.  A feature inspired by your idea is in the product pipeline
  • Answered - Your Idea is either functionality we already have available, or not something we can facilitate, and we’ll provide further information within the post.

We aim to provide an initial status update to all Ideas marked ‘no status’ within 5 working days.  From there it’s up to our community of voters to help our Product Teams determine what’s next!  Unfortunately, our team won’t be able to comment on each individual idea, and some ideas may not be taken forward but our Product team and community of customers are always reviewing your ideas to influence how Fourth can develop and evolve our products for the benefit of all of our customers.

Voting

If you see an existing Idea from another Fourth user that you think would also work well for your business, please ‘Vote’ on the idea so it can help inspire our Product Team.

Select the title of the post, and then select the upwards facing arrow to vote in favour of the suggested idea. You can vote for as many ideas you think are important!  Thanks for providing us some valuable feedback as to how we can evolve your Fourth Solution!

posts.title: Welcome to Ideas - Click for Full Details
posts.details:
Welcome to Ideas

This is our area specifically designed for our customers to post any suggestions for changes to the Mobile & Apps solution. To help us review your suggestions, please follow the information areas below.  We’ve also created a short step-by-step process to make it easy to start suggesting!   

Creating an Idea

  • Select 'New Post' in the top right corner
  • Ensure 'Ideas: P2P Mobile Apps' is selected as the Topic underneath the details box

When entering details about your suggested idea in the 'Details' field, please be sure to include the following information:

  • Business Requirement (Why is this change needed? What challenge does it address?)
  • Suggested Changes (How can this address your Business Requirement? What benefit will it bring?)

Your Idea will then be reviewed by our team and will be marked as one of the following:

  • No Status –Your idea has been received! Our team are currently reviewing your Idea and will be in touch shortly. 
  • Open for Voting – Your Idea has been validated by our experts, get voting! The Product Decision team will periodically review the ideas and any ideas selected to progress further, will have more detail provided once available.
  • Planned- Congratulations! Your ideas was selected and will form part of our near-term development strategy.  A feature inspired by your idea is in the product pipeline
  • Answered - Your Idea is either functionality we already have available, or not something we can facilitate, and we’ll provide further information within the post.
  • Completed –Inspirational! Your Idea helped our teams design and release a new development.  It has now been published as a release, along with a copy of the release note in your original post.  Enjoy!   

We aim to provide an initial status update to all Ideas marked ‘no status’ within 5 working days.  From there it’s up to our community of voters to help our Product Teams determine what’s next!  Unfortunately, our team won’t be able to comment on each individual idea, and some ideas may not be taken forward but our Product team and community of customers are always reviewing your ideas to influence how Fourth can develop and evolve our products for the benefit of all of our customers.

Voting

If you see an existing Idea from another Fourth user that you think would also work well for your business, please ‘Vote’ on the idea so it can help inspire our Product Team.

Select the title of the post, and then select the upwards facing arrow to vote in favour of the suggested idea. You can vote for as many ideas you think are important!  Thanks for providing us some valuable feedback as to how we can evolve your Fourth Solution!

posts.title: Calander invite incorpoarted into posts/annoucements/ banners
posts.details:
Current standard process

The Internal Comms team co-ordinate internal events for all employees.

They are often Team Live events but can also use Webex, or be scheduled Zoom events

Internal Comms will create a link to an event (open URL) and then promote heavily via existing comms channels

Current non-standard process

For the recent pride panel event, comms sent out as an Outlook invite to Corporate and Field based employees. This was not planned, but due to a specific issue which meant the original comms link would not work.

This calendar approach created a much greater level of attendance, and was the instigator for this request (c.200 attendees).

Using the outlook approach will create more admin and cannot be used for Team Players (or anyone without a GK email address) as there is no BCC option in sending meeting invites. This may also be a PECR issue.

Objective

Increase attendance for internal events, by giving employees the tools to automatically add events to their own calendar and set reminders. This could be via a registration or a simple add to calendar option.

posts.title: RME - GET API Suggested Change Recipe Nutrition

posts.author: Ian Smith

comments.author: Leslie Grogan
comments.body:
Hi 397273794191

In RME, 'salt' is calculated 'on the fly' based on the sodium value.  While 'sodium' is stored in the database, 'salt' does not exist in the database as a separate value and therefore does not have a separate GUID.

As we are unlikely to change this in the near future, third parties using the RME nutrition information might find integrations easier if they chose either the sodium or the salt value.

Best regards

Leslie

posts.title: Point Based Attendance System
posts.details:
It would be a huge operational win if a point based attendance system was implemented in hotschedules. 

System I'm most familiar with - 

Employees Start with 10 Points

Employees Gain 1 Point a Month with Perfect Attendance 

Late under <15 minutes: Deduction of 0.5 points

Late over >15 minutes: Deduction of 1 points

Shift Call Out with at least 30 minutes notice - Deduction of 2 Points

No Call No Show - Deduction of 5 Points

If the employee reaches 0 points, they're terminated.

 

I love hotschedules, but this is a huge selling point for competitors that offer that functionality. As a customer, I want to have accountability for attendance built into my scheduling system. 

Thank you for the consideration!

The payroll preview is a large report that performs payroll and pension calculations as it runs, so it does run slightly slower than some other reports.  Doing the calculations this way allows us to have a real time system without the requirement to re-calculate separately after each change.

Ali

posts.title: Recruiting Data Gathering
posts.details:
Hello, 

I noticed that hotschedules collects data from team members regarding how many hours they would like to work at a minimum and how many hours they would like to work maximum in their "Employee Threshold" Category when inputting their availability. I inquired about finding a report that would allow me and my team to quickly see this data in bulk and there is not a report available.

Being able to access this data in bulk would help tremendously with forecasting how many people we need to recruit for the upcoming months. We would be able to see how many hours our team wants to work vs how many are available in real time and forecasted out. 

Hotschedules is already collecting this data, why not enhance your service by making it available to us to harvest and utilize at our discretion. If you took it further, you could also break it down by daypart in the future and really help our recruiting forecasting.  But honestly, just being able to see the number of hours my team wants to work in bulk would help right away. Right now, we are creating our own system to collect this data but I hope hotschedules will consider adding this feature. Everyone is in a crunch in recruiting and this only helps your value prop. Thanks!

posts.author: Jovita Paraskevopoulou

comments.author: Nicola Kibble
comments.body: Hi.  Thanks for your question.  Absence types will only pay SSP or CSP (set up through Contracts) automatically.  The absence type that's been created to record a sabbatical will appear on the rota/schedule as 'Absent' and will deduct any salary for the associated absence period.  The payment in lieu of normal salary will need to be added to the employee as an additional payment.

posts.title: Tradesimple: Line-Level Tolerances on Invoice Discrepancies
posts.details:
We use the "Manage Invoice Discrepancy" tool in Tradesimple.

Currently, we have configured a tolerance value for the total invoice price difference but would like to set a tolerance value for each line item.

For example, if line item difference is within tolerance, action can be set automatically to mark "Invoice is right". If all line items are within the tolerance, the invoice discrepancy should be processed automatically.
posts.author: Scott Owens

comments.author: Fourth Customer Success Portal
comments.body:
Hi 412756021052,

We believe that this may already be possible in Tradesimple by applying some settings. We're just checking with our system experts and will get back to you as soon as possible.

Best wishes,
Fourth Communities Team

comments.author: Scott Owens
comments.body:
Hi, could I get an update from the system experts please?

 

Scott

comments.author: Fourth Customer Success Portal
comments.body:
Hi 412756021052,

Sorry not to get back to you sooner on this. We have the following for you:

We should already be able to do this. We have two settings on Tradesimple that can be activated at the same time:
  1. Line-level tolerance - Defined as a percentage of the invoice line total. It is computed against each invoice line. If any of the lines fails the check, that is, if the difference is greater than the tolerance,  it will throw a discrepancy.
  2. Total Value tolerance - This is an absolute value, checked against the Total Amount.

This setting is not accessible from the front-end so you will need to raise a support ticket to request for it to be done. We can see that your organisation already have settings in place for both of these, so that will be something to enquire about when raising your support ticket - we will not post that information here.

Hope this helps, and apologies again for the delay.

Best,
Fourth Communities Team.

posts.title: Trade Simple Cumulative spend calculation in Order Authorisation feature
posts.details:
We believe there is an issue with the cumulative spend calculation that is seen on the Order authorisation screen in Trade Simple and in Ordering (My example just uses screen grabs from Trade SImple, but the same can be seen in ordering)


Essentially the cumulative spend calculation that is displayed should sum up order values, by using the most recent document in the thread, and not just the initial order value. Reason being is that due to availability issues suppliers may not invoice for the full value as they are unable to deliver all items on the order, therefore the invoice value is lower than the order value and this should be reflected in the cumulative spend total calculation that is displayed on screen within the order authorisation feature.
Please see example below.

Order placed for £404.36 at start of a budget period

After the order is placed but before the invoice lands in the thread, the site is showing a cumulative spend in the period as shown below – This is the £404.36 from the order above, plus the order just about to be placed of £23.22 – giving a total spend in the period of £427.58

However, once the order is invoiced by the supplier, we can see what was actually delivered to the site. In this case £366.13 was invoiced

We would therefore expect for the cumulative total spend in the period to be adjusted down by. But when we back into place an order and see the Authorisation message we still see that the cumulative spend includes the £404.36 and not the £366.13.
posts.author: Simon Madders

comments.author: Fourth Customer Success Portal
comments.body:
Hey 397187114452,

As discussed with your team, as starting point we have agreed to look at the logic on how we calculate the cumulative spend and then get an agreement if it is the right or a change is required. 

Thanks,
Fourth Communities Team

posts.title: Can I configure HotSchedules calendar to show Sunday as the start of every week?
posts.details:
Hi, new to HotSchedules, my company is trying to adopt it for scheduling to make life for management easier.  I am an end user (client) not in management. 

Is there a way I can configure the interface in HotSchedules so the calendar always shows a particular day of the week (e.g. Sunday) as the left-most box?  I believe HS's "rolling start-day calendar" view, where the first day shown on the left is the current day of the week, is not a particularly intuitive UX decision.

I can tell the rolling start-day calendar was meant to be helpful, but this is not how calendars usually operate.  If people are used to seeing all calendars look a certain way, it's easy to assume the one in HotSchedules would be, too.  Since HS calendar shows a different left-most box for every day of the week, I am concerned it will result in user error.

Some people may like the rolling start-day calendar, but if there was some way I as a user could set the left-most box of the calendar to Sunday (or, some people like Monday) and always stay that way regardless of what day of the week it is, that would be extremely helpful for me personally.  Is that possible?

Thank you,

Avery
posts.author: Avery Freeman

comments.author: Chris Sundgren
comments.body:
Hi Avery, 

Thanks for the post. The calendar view of your schedule matches your companies scheduling week which I believe is Tuesday to Monday. During the design phase of your schedule view, our UX team wanted to ensure you could see your entire scheduling week since that's how schedules are posted. Trying to follow a standard calendar week would break up this view for those that don't do traditional Sun-Sat scheduling.

Thanks again for the post and please keep feedback coming our way!!
